akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾: an oath upon ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ [4].

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾: He did not mention "that it is a return"; that is — and Allah knows best — because it was in answer, as though it had been said to them: "You will return". So they said: "When we have become dust? That is a far return."

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ because you say: "لَبَسْتُ عليه لَبْساً" (I confused it for him).

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾: He means "more in control of him and nearer to him in power over him".

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾ and did not say "on the right a seated one and on the left a seated one"; He mentioned one of them and it sufficed, as He said ﴿يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلاً﴾, where the singular sufficed for the plural, and as He said ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً﴾.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿ق﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ﴾ the noble: the disbelievers of Mecca did not believe in Muhammad ﷺ ﴿بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جَاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ a messenger from among themselves making them fear the Fire after the resurrection ﴿فَقَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ هَذَا﴾ warning ﴿شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿أَإِذَا﴾ with both hamzas fully pronounced (taḥqīq), and with lightening (tashīl) of the second, and with an alif inserted between them in both ways ﴿مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا﴾ shall we return? ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ﴾ extremely far-fetched.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ eats ﴿مِنْهُمْ وَعِنْدَنَا كِتَابٌ حَفِيظٌ﴾ it is the Preserved Tablet, in which are all things decreed.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the Quran ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ فَهُمْ﴾ concerning the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran ﴿فِي أَمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ﴾ confused: once they said "a sorcerer" and "sorcery", once "a poet" and "poetry", and once "a soothsayer" and "soothsaying".

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا﴾ with their eyes, taking a lesson with their minds, when they denied the resurrection ﴿إِلَى السَّمَاءِ﴾ being ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَاهَا﴾ without pillars ﴿وَزَيَّنَّاهَا﴾ with the stars ﴿وَمَا لَهَا مِنْ فُرُوجٍ﴾ cracks that would mar it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to the position of «إِلَى السَّمَاءِ»; how ﴿مَدَدْنَاهَا﴾ We spread it out on the surface of the water ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ﴾ mountains that make it firm ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ﴾ kind ﴿بَهِيجٍ﴾ which delights because of its beauty.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿تَبْصِرَةً﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. We did that as an enlightening from Us ﴿وَذِكْرَى﴾ a reminding ﴿لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾ who returns often to obedience to Us.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُبَارَكًا﴾ of abundant blessing ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنَا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ orchards ﴿وَحَبَّ﴾ of the crop ﴿الْحَصِيدِ﴾ that is harvested.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَالنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ﴾ tall; an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) ﴿لَهَا طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ﴾ piled one upon another.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿رِزْقًا لِلْعِبَادِ﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) ﴿وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا﴾ in which the masculine and the feminine are alike ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like this giving of life ﴿الْخُرُوجُ﴾ from the graves; so how can you deny it? The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), and the meaning is that they looked and knew what has been mentioned.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾ the verb is feminine because of the meaning of «قَوْم» ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ الرَّسِّ﴾ it is a well at which they stayed with their livestock, worshipping idols; their prophet, it is said, was Ḥanẓala ibn Ṣafwān, and it is said someone else ﴿وَثَمُودُ﴾ the people of Ṣāliḥ

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَعَادٌ﴾ the people of Hūd ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَانُ لُوطٍ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ﴾ i.e. the thicket; the people of Shuʿayb ﴿وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾ he was a king in Yemen who became Muslim and called his people to Islam, and they denied him ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of those mentioned ﴿كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ﴾ like Quraysh ﴿فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ﴾ the descent of the punishment upon all became binding, so let not your breast be constricted by the disbelief of Quraysh in you.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿أَفَعَيِينَا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ﴾ i.e. We were not wearied by it, so We will not be wearied by the repetition ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ doubt ﴿مِنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ and it is the resurrection.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «نَحْنُ» implied ﴿مَا﴾ maṣdariyya (infinitival) ﴿تُوَسْوِسُ﴾ speaks ﴿بِهِ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) or for making the verb transitive, and the pronoun refers to man ﴿نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ﴾ in knowledge ﴿مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ﴾ the genitive construct is explicative (bayān); the two warīds are two veins on the two sides of the neck.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ what puts it in the accusative is an implied «اذْكُرْ» (remember) ﴿يَتَلَقَّى﴾ takes and records ﴿الْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ﴾ the two angels assigned to man, what he does ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ﴾ of him ﴿قَعِيدٌ﴾ i.e. two sitting ones; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is what precedes it.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ﴾ a guardian ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾ present; and each of them has the meaning of the dual.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ its overwhelming and its severity ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ of the matter of the Hereafter, so that the one who denied it sees it with his own eyes; and it is the severity itself ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. death ﴿مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ﴾ flee and take fright.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ for the resurrection ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the day of the blowing ﴿يَوْمُ الْوَعِيدِ﴾ for the disbelievers, with punishment.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ﴾ on it ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ to the place of gathering ﴿مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ﴾ an angel who drives it there ﴿وَشَهِيدٌ﴾ who testifies against it regarding its deeds, and it is the hands, the feet and others; and it will be said to the disbeliever:

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كُنْتَ﴾ in this world ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا﴾ which descends on you today ﴿فَكَشَفْنَا عَنْكَ غِطَاءَكَ﴾ We removed your heedlessness by what you witness today ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾ sharp, by which you perceive what you denied in this world.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ the angel assigned to him ﴿هَذَا مَا﴾ i.e. that which ﴿لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾ present; then it will be said to Mālik:

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾ i.e. «أَلْقِ أَلْقِ» ("throw, throw"), or «أَلْقِيَنْ», and al-Ḥasan read it so; the nūn was then changed into an alif ﴿كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾ obstinate against the truth

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ such as zakat ﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾ unjust ﴿مُرِيبٍ﴾ doubting his religion

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) made to include the meaning of a condition; its khabar (predicate) is ﴿فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي الْعَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ﴾ its explanation is like what has preceded.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿قَالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ the devil ﴿رَبَّنَا مَا أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾ I did not lead him astray ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَانَ فِي ضَلَالٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾ so I called him and he answered me; and he [the man] said: "He led me astray by calling me."

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ He, Exalted is He ﴿لَا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ﴾ i.e. disputing is of no benefit here ﴿وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ in this world ﴿بِالْوَعِيدِ﴾ with punishment in the Hereafter if you did not believe, and it is inevitable.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿مَا يُبَدَّلُ﴾ is changed ﴿الْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ﴾ in that ﴿وَمَا أَنَا بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ so as to punish them without a crime; «ظَلَّام» is in the meaning of «ذُو ظُلْم» (one possessing injustice), because of His saying {لَا ظُلْمَ الْيَوْمَ}.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ what puts it in the accusative is «ظَلَّام» ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ ﴿لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ﴾ an interrogative confirming His promise to fill it ﴿وَتَقُولُ﴾ in the form of an interrogative, like a question ﴿هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ﴾ i.e. in me; I cannot hold more than what I have been filled with, i.e. I am already full.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ﴾ was brought near ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ to a place ﴿غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾ from them, so they see it, and it will be said to them:

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ which is seen ﴿مَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ, in this world; and His saying ﴿لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ﴾ is a badal (substitute) of «لِلْمُتَّقِينَ»; one who returns often to obedience to Allah ﴿حَفِيظٍ﴾ who guards His limits

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ feared Him without having seen Him ﴿وَجَاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾ turning to His obedience; and it will also be said to the God-fearing:

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ﴾ i.e. safe from every fear, or with peace, i.e. give greetings of peace and enter ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the day on which the entry took place ﴿يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ﴾ permanence in the Garden.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿لَهُمْ مَا يَشَاءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ﴾ an addition beyond what they did and asked for.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ i.e. We destroyed before the disbelievers of Quraysh many generations of disbelievers ﴿هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشًا﴾ in strength ﴿فَنَقَّبُوا﴾ they searched ﴿فِي الْبِلَادِ هَلْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾ for them or for others from death; and they found none.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ mentioned ﴿لَذِكْرَى﴾ an admonition ﴿لِمَنْ كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾ a mind ﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ﴾ listened to the admonition ﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ present with the heart.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ the first of them Sunday and the last Friday ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ﴾ weariness. It was revealed as a rebuttal of the Jews in their saying that Allah rested on Saturday. Weariness is negated of Him because He, Exalted is He, is far above the attributes of created beings, and because there is no contact between Him and anything else: {إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ}

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ addressed to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the Jews and others, of likening [Allah to creation] and denial ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ pray, praising ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ i.e. the dawn prayer ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ i.e. the noon and afternoon prayers.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ i.e. pray the two night prayers (al-ʿishāʾān) ﴿وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of «دُبُر», and with kasra on it [إِدْبَارَ], the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَدْبَرَ»; i.e. pray the recommended voluntary prayers after the obligatory ones. And it is said: what is meant is actual glorification (tasbīḥ) at these times, accompanied by praise.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ O you addressed, to what I say ﴿يَوْمَ يُنَادِ الْمُنَادِ﴾ he is Isrāfīl ﴿مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾ to the sky, and it is the Rock of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), the place on earth nearest to the sky. He will say: "O decayed bones, severed joints, torn flesh and scattered hairs! Allah commands you to gather together for the final judgement."

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of «يَوْمَ» before it ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ i.e. all creatures ﴿الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with the resurrection, and it is the second blowing by Isrāfīl; and it may be before his call or after it ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the day of the calling and the hearing ﴿يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ﴾ from the graves. What puts «يَوْمَ يُنَادِي» in the accusative is implied, i.e. «يَعْلَمُونَ عَاقِبَةَ تَكْذِيبِهِمْ» ("they will know the outcome of their denial").

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of «يَوْمَ» before it, and what is between them is parenthetical ﴿تَشَقَّقُ﴾ with the shīn light and doubled, by assimilating the second tāʾ of the underlying form into it ﴿الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا﴾ the plural of «سَرِيع»; a ḥāl (circumstantial) from something implied, i.e. «فَيَخْرُجُونَ مُسْرِعِينَ» ("so they come out hastening") ﴿ذَلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ﴾ in it the described noun and its adjective are separated by what the adjective is attached to, for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and that does no harm. «ذَلِكَ» points to the meaning of the gathering that is reported about it, namely giving life after annihilation and the gathering for presentation and reckoning.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Quraysh ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾ to compel them to believe; and this was before the command for jihad ﴿فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ﴾ and they are the believers.

daas-irab:1-7.t: ﴿ق﴾ a letter with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْقُرْآنِ﴾ the wāw is a particle, and of oath [Translator's note: so in the source, «حرف وقسم»; presumably "a particle of oath and genitive"]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb. ﴿الْمَجِيدِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the answer to the oath is omitted. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿عَجِبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مُنْذِرٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to منذر; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿عَجِيبٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَإِذا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and إذا is an adverbial conditional particle not governing the jussive. ﴿مِتْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَكُنَّا تُراباً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ رَجْعٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿بَعِيدٌ﴾ an adjective. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its mafʿūl; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَعِنْدَنا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿كِتابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿حَفِيظٌ﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression and transition. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ adverbial, of time ("when"). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي أَمْرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَرِيجٍ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and lam is a jussive particle. ﴿يَنْظُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَى السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, ḥāl. ﴿بَنَيْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is a badal (substitute) from السماء. ﴿وَزَيَّنَّاها﴾ conjoined to بنيناها. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and mā is negating. ﴿لَها﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿فُرُوجٍ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and الأرض is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "مددنا الأرض". ﴿مَدَدْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنا﴾ conjoined to مددنا. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنا﴾ conjoined to ألقينا. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿زَوْجٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَهِيجٍ﴾ an adjective of زوج.

daas-irab:8-15.t: ﴿تَبْصِرَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَذِكْرى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تبصرة. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تبصرة. ﴿عَبْدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُنِيبٍ﴾ an adjective of عبد. ﴿وَنَزَّلْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُبارَكاً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَحَبَّ﴾ conjoined to جنات. ﴿الْحَصِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالنَّخْلَ﴾ conjoined to جنات. ﴿باسِقاتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra. ﴿لَها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿طَلْعٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَضِيدٌ﴾ an adjective of طلع; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi, accusative. ﴿لِلْعِبادِ﴾ the two are attached to it. ﴿وَأَحْيَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿بَلْدَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَيْتاً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿الْخُرُوجُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذَّبَتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb. ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَصْحابُ﴾ conjoined to قوم. ﴿الرَّسِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَثَمُودُ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوانُ لُوطٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الرُّسُلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فَحَقَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿وَعِيدِ﴾ its fāʿil, and the omitted yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَفَعَيِينا﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِالْخَلْقِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَوَّلِ﴾ an adjective; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ خَلْقٍ﴾ the two are attached to لبس. ﴿جَدِيدٍ﴾ an adjective of خلق.

daas-irab:16-21.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the answer to an oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "نحن", and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تُوَسْوِسُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نَفْسُهُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to أقرب. ﴿مِنْ حَبْلِ﴾ the two are also attached to أقرب. ﴿الْوَرِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يَتَلَقَّى﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْمُتَلَقِّيانِ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ﴾ the two are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿قَعِيدٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يَلْفِظُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause ما يلفظ is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ قَوْلٍ﴾ a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and a noun genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لَدَيْهِ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿رَقِيبٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾ badal (substitute); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَجاءَتْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a past verb. ﴿سَكْرَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ذلِكَ ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to تحيد. ﴿تَحِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of كنت, and the clause كنت is the ṣila of mā and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَنُفِخَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْوَعِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَجاءَتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَعَها﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿سائِقٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَشَهِيدٌ﴾ conjoined to سائق; the nominal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of كل.

daas-irab:22-28.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ هذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) غفلة. ﴿فَكَشَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَنْكَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غِطاءَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿حَدِيدٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿هذا ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾ an adjective of mā. ﴿أَلْقِيا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَّارٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَنِيدٍ﴾ an adjective of كفار; the verbal clause is the object of saying. ﴿مَنَّاعٍ﴾ a second adjective of كفار. ﴿لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to مناع. ﴿مُعْتَدٍ مُرِيبٍ﴾ two further adjectives of كفار. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ badal (substitute) from كل. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آخَرَ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فَأَلْقِياهُ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the alif is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its mafʿūl; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الشَّدِيدِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿قالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a vocative (munādā) in construct. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ the khabar of kāna. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لا تَخْتَصِمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying, and the clause قال is resumptive. ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a particle of verification. ﴿قَدَّمْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿بِالْوَعِيدِ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:29-35.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يُبَدَّلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنَا﴾ its noun. ﴿بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of mā. ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظلام; the clause of mā is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to ظلام. ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِجَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿هَلِ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿امْتَلَأْتِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَتَقُولُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿هَلِ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿مِنْ مَزِيدٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and مزيد is genitive in form, nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الْجَنَّةُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هذا ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a badal (substitute) from His words للمتقين. ﴿أَوَّابٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَفِيظٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a badal from كل. ﴿خَشِيَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الرَّحْمنَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَجاءَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِقَلْبٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مُنِيبٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿ادْخُلُوها﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and hā its mafʿūl; the clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿بِسَلامٍ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْخُلُودِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿ما﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَشاؤُنَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿وَلَدَيْنا﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿مَزِيدٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-39.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and kam is predicative (khabariyya), an advanced mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and قرن is genitive in form, accusative in position, a tamyīz (specification). ﴿هُمْ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an adjective of قرن. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد. ﴿بَطْشاً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿فَنَقَّبُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْبِلادِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿هَلْ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾ a redundant particle, and محيص is genitive in form, nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿لَذِكْرى﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and ذكرى is the noun of inna; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of ذكرى. ﴿كانَ لَهُ﴾ kāna and its advanced khabar. ﴿قَلْبٌ﴾ its postponed noun; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَلْقَى﴾ a past verb. ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification. ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ its mafʿūl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿فِي سِتَّةِ﴾ the two are attached to خلقنا. ﴿أَيَّامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and mā is negating. ﴿مَسَّنا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿مِنْ لُغُوبٍ﴾ min is a redundant preposition, and a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of مسنا; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ conjoined to اصبر. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿طُلُوعِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:40-45.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبح. ﴿فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿وَأَدْبارَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يُنادِ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْمُنادِ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يوم. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الصَّيْحَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْخُرُوجِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿نُحْيِي﴾ an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَنُمِيتُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نحيي. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إلينا is an advanced khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal from يوم يسمعون. ﴿تَشَقَّقُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿سِراعاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿يَسِيرٌ﴾ an adjective of حشر; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿بِجَبَّارٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and جبار is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالْقُرْآنِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَعِيدِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila of man, and the clause ذكر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرِيجٍ): unsettled, in disorder. Its origin is from motion and disturbance; hence maraja al-khātam fī iṣbaʿihi ("the ring wobbled on his finger") when it is loose from thinness. In al-Mukhtār: «maraja al-amr wa-l-dīn: the matter and the religion became confused; its verb pattern is ṭariba; and amr marīj means a confused matter.» The meaning is that they do not hold firm to one opinion: at one time they say "a poet", at another "a sorcerer", at another "a soothsayer".

* I'rab:
(ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ): The discussion of the openings of the sūras has already preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; القرآن is the thing sworn by; المجيد is an adjective. The answer to the oath is omitted, indicated by what follows it, and its implied form is "you came to them warning of the resurrection, and they did not accept but were amazed". It is also said that it is mentioned, and they differed over its implied form: it is said to be «قد علمنا», and it is said to be His words «ما يلفظ من قول». The first is preferable and more firmly rooted in rhetoric. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "you will surely be resurrected" or "you will surely be returned", in accordance with what the context of the verses indicates.
(بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَقالَ الْكافِرُونَ هذا شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ): بل is a particle of conjunction and of retraction (iḍrāb); it breaks off from the omitted answer to the oath in order to explain their state, which is even more shameful and ugly. عجبوا is verb and agent; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "at the fact that there came to them". منذر is the agent of جاءهم and منهم is an adjective of منذر. فقال: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال الكافرون is verb and agent; هذا is the mubtadaʾ, شيء the khabar and عجيب an adjective; the clause is the content of the saying.
(أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً ذلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ): The hamza is for denunciatory interrogation. إذا is an adverbial (ẓarf) for the future time, containing the sense of a condition; متنا is verb and agent, and the clause متنا is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The governor of the adverb is implied, its sense being "When we die and decay, shall we be returned?", because what follows indicates it. كنا is kāna with its ism, and ترابا is its khabar. ذلك is the mubtadaʾ, رجع the khabar and بعيد an adjective, meaning "deemed improbable and objectionable", from your saying "this is a far-off speech", i.e. far from imagination and custom.
(قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ وَعِنْدَنا كِتابٌ حَفِيظٌ): A resumptive discourse, brought in to refute their deeming improbable something that is close to the understanding of the believers, whose breasts Allah has opened. قد is a particle of certainty; علمنا is verb and agent; ما is a relative noun, direct object; the clause تنقص الأرض is the ṣila; منهم is attached to تنقص. The wāw is circumstantial; عندنا is an adverbial attached to an omitted advanced khabar; كتاب is a delayed mubtadaʾ; حفيظ is an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl.
(بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ فَهُمْ فِي أَمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ): بل is a particle of retraction, a retraction of transition from what is shameful to what is more shameful and ugly, namely denying prophethood after denying the resurrection. كذبوا is verb and agent; بالحق is attached to كذبوا; لما is a temporal adverbial of time, or a connective. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is the mubtadaʾ; أمر is the khabar and مريج an adjective.
(أَفَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا إِلَى السَّماءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْناها وَزَيَّنَّاها وَما لَها مِنْ فُرُوجٍ): The hamza is for denunciatory interrogation, and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted clause that sweeps away everything they said in encroachment on the truth and denial of it, i.e. "Were they heedless and did they act so that they did not look?". لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; إلى السماء is attached to ينظروا; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; بنيناها is verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is a substitute (badal) for السماء. The wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; لها is an advanced khabar; من is a redundant preposition; فروج is genitive in form, a delayed mubtadaʾ in position. فروج means cracks, fissures and clefts, and it is the plural of farj.
(وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْناها وَأَلْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ): The wāw is a conjunction; الأرض is conjoined to the position of إلى السماء, which is the accusative as a direct object. You may also put الأرض in the accusative by an omitted verb, the implied form being "and We spread out the earth"; on the first view the clause مددناها is circumstantial. ألقينا is conjoined to مددنا; فيها is attached to ألقينا; and رواسي is the direct object, i.e. firmly set, fixed mountains.
(وَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ): وأنبتنا is also conjoined to what precedes; فيها is attached to أنبتنا, and من كل زوج is also attached to أنبتنا; بهيج is an adjective of زوج.
(تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرى لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ): تبصرة and ذكرى are objects of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi). It is also said that they are accusative by an implied verb of their own root, i.e. as absolute objects (mafʿūl muṭlaq); and it is said that they are two ḥāls of the agent, i.e. "making to see and reminding", or a ḥāl of the direct object, i.e. "possessing insight and possessing reminder". لكل is attached to تبصرة and to ذكرى; عبد is a muḍāf ilayhi; منيب is an adjective of عبد.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words from «ق» to «عجيب» there is the art of tasjīʿ (rhymed prose), or "isjāʿ". This is a long subject on which the scholars of this art composed lengthy books. It is that the speaker takes care to give his sentences rhymed prose. It is of two kinds: one in which the rhymed sentences come summarily, embedded among the unrhymed sentences; and one in which the rhymed sentences come on their own. An example of the first is the saying of ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ghayyāth al-Ḥimṣī, known as Dīk al-Jinn: «ḥurr al-ihāb wasīmuh, barr al-iyāb karīmuh, maḥḍ al-nisāb ḥamīmuh» (free in skin and handsome, righteous on return and noble, pure in lineage and loyal). The second kind will be mentioned in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.
2- In His words «المجيد» there is a figurative attribution (majāz bi-l-isnād), because it is the state of the speaker: whoever knows its rulings and aims and complies with its commands and prohibitions becomes glorious.

dervis-irab:9-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَصِيدِ): that which is of the nature of being harvested.
(باسِقاتٍ): busūq means height. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «basaqat al-nakhla busūqan (from the pattern of qaʿada): the palm grew tall, so it is bāsiqa, and the plural is bāsiqāt and bawāsiq. Basaqa al-rajul: the man became skilled in his work.» The poet said:
لنا خمر وليست خمر كرم ... ولكن من نتاج الباسقات
كرام في السماء ذهبن طولا ... وفات ثمارها أيدي الجناة
(We have a wine, though it is not wine of the vine, but from the yield of the tall ones; noble ones that went high into the sky in height, their fruit beyond the hands of the pickers.) And from the use in the second meaning is the saying of Ibn Nawfal about Ibn Hubayra:
يا ابن الذين بمجدهم ... بسقت على قيس فزاره
(O son of those by whose glory you rose high above Qays and Fazāra.)
(نَضِيدٌ): piled up, one part on top of another. The explanation of the meaning of ṭalʿ (spathe) has already preceded in His words, Exalted is He, «ومن طلعها قنوان».
(أَفَعَيِينا): from ʿayiya bi-l-amr, when one is not guided to the way of knowing it. ʿayiya ʿan ḥujjatihi yaʿyā (from the pattern ʿayā): he was unable to produce it. The past tense is sometimes assimilated, so that one says ʿayya; so the man is ʿayyin or ʿayiyun, on the patterns fa-ʿil and faʿīl. ʿayiya bi-l-amr: he was not guided to its way. aʿyānī, with alif: it tired me out; so aʿyaytu is used both transitively and intransitively; and aʿyā in his walking, so he is muʿyin (defective). In al-Mukhtār: «al-ʿayy is the opposite of clear expression. ʿayiya fī manṭiqihi, so he is ʿayyun, on the pattern faʿil; and ʿayiya yaʿyā, on the pattern of raḍiya yarḍā, so he is ʿayīyun on the pattern faʿīl. One also says ʿayyun and ʿayīyun when he is not guided to its way, and assimilation is more common; and aʿyāhu amruhu.»
(لَبْسٍ): doubt, confusion, uncertainty.

* I'rab:
(وَنَزَّلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً مُبارَكاً فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ وَحَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ): The wāw is a conjunction; نزلنا is verb and agent; من السماء is attached to نزلنا; ماء is the direct object and مباركا an adjective. فأنبتنا is conjoined to نزلنا; به is attached to أنبتنا; جنات is the direct object; and حب الحصيد is conjoined to جنات, i.e. "and the grain of the crop that is harvested", the described noun having been omitted.
(وَالنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ): والنخل is conjoined to جنات and حب الحصيد; باسقات is an implied ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of growing they were not tall; لها is an advanced khabar; طلع is a delayed mubtadaʾ; نضيد is an adjective of طلع; and the clause is a ḥāl of النخل الباسقات by way of succession, or of the pronoun in باسقات by way of embedding.
(رِزْقاً لِلْعِبادِ وَأَحْيَيْنا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً كَذلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ): In رزقا it is permissible that it be an object of purpose, or an absolute object as a maṣdar from the sense of أنبتنا, or a ḥāl, i.e. "provided for the servants" or "possessing provision". للعباد is an adjective of رزقا and attached to it as a maṣdar. وأحيينا is conjoined to فأنبتنا; به is attached to أحيينا; بلدة is the direct object and ميتا an adjective. كذلك is an advanced khabar and الخروج a delayed mubtadaʾ; the khabar is advanced for restriction (ḥaṣr).
(كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَأَصْحابُ الرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ): A resumptive discourse to explain a present reality concerning the resurrection and the agreement of all the messengers upon it. قبلهم is an adverbial attached to كذبت; قوم نوح is the agent; and what follows it is conjoined to it.
(وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوانُ لُوطٍ): also conjoined to what precedes.
(وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ): also conjoined; all of these have already been covered.
(كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ): كل is the mubtadaʾ, and the tanwīn in it is a substitute for a word, i.e. "every messenger of those mentioned"; the clause كذب الرسل is its khabar. The fāʾ is a conjunction; حق is a past verb; وعيد is the agent, annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, its origin being وعيدي, and the yāʾ was dropped, the kasra remaining as an indication of it.
(أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ): The hamza is for interrogation, i.e. "were We not unable regarding it, so that We would be unable in repeating it?". The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted clause whose implied form is "Did We intend the creation and then fail at it, so that anyone could imagine Our incapacity to repeat it?". عيينا is verb and agent; بالخلق is attached to عيينا; الأول is an adjective of الخلق. بل is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, brought in to explain their confusion and expose their sophistry, the implied form being "they do not deny Our power, but they are in confusion and doubt". هم is the mubtadaʾ; في لبس is the khabar; من خلق is an adjective of لبس; and جديد is an adjective of خلق.

* Rhetoric:
Definiteness and indefiniteness: in the definiteness of "the first creation" and the indefiniteness of "confusion" and "a new creation" there are miraculous rhetorical purposes. The definiteness is a distinguishing of the magnificence of what is intended to be made definite, and a glorification of it; likewise the definiteness of "males" in His words, Exalted is He, «ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور». The aim of it is to make it evidence of the possibility of the second creation a fortiori: for if He, Exalted is He, was not incapacitated by the creation, despite its greatness, vastness and comprehensiveness of what bewilders minds and perplexes thoughts, then the other creation is a mere repetition, which is more fitting to be paid no regard and not to exceed the range of power and possibility. This is the secret of the definiteness of the first creation. As for indefiniteness, its matter is divided. At times what is intended by it is the magnification of the indefinite thing, from the vagueness within it, as though it were too magnificent to be addressed by a definite form; and at times what is intended is belittling the indefinite thing and lowering it. An example of the first is His words, Exalted is He, «سلام قولا من رب رحيم», and His words «لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم», and His words «إن المتقين في جنات ونعيم»; it is too much to count. The second is the basic function of indefiniteness and needs no illustration. So the indefiniteness of "confusion" is from exaltation and magnification, as though He said: "in a [grave] confusion"; and the indefiniteness of "a new creation" is for belittling it and making light of its matter in relation to the first creation. It may also be for magnification, as though it were a matter too great for a person to be content with its being obscure to him, when the first thing in which he observes its soundness ... [Translator's note: the source sentence ends abruptly, «وأنه أول ما تبصر فيه صحته», as printed; translated as written.]

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُوَسْوِسُ): al-waswasa is a hidden sound, and from it comes the waswās of ornaments. The waswasa of the soul is what passes through a person's mind and stirs in his inner self of the self-talk of the soul.
(حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The "jugular vein" (ḥabl al-warīd) is a proverbial expression for extreme nearness, like their saying "he is to me the place where the midwife ties" and "the place where the waist-wrapper is tied". Dhū al-Rumma said:
هل أغدونّ في عيشة رغيد ... والموت أدنى لي من الوريد
(Shall I go out in the morning into an easy life, when death is nearer to me than the jugular vein?) that is: I shall not be in a spacious life, since death is nearer to me than the jugular vein. The two warīds are two veins at the front of the two sides of the neck, so called because they come down (yaridān) from the head, or because the spirit comes to them (tariduhumā). The discussion of the reason for annexing ḥabl to al-warīd has already preceded.»
(عَتِيدٌ): present. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «ʿatuda al-shayʾ (with ḍamma), ʿatādan (with fatḥa): it was present; so it is ʿatid (with two fatḥas) and also ʿatīd. It becomes transitive with hamza and with doubling, so one says aʿtadahu ṣāḥibuhu and ʿattadahu when he prepared it and made it ready. In the Revelation: «وأعتدت لهنّ متكأ».»

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ): The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; خلقنا الإنسان is a past verb, agent and direct object. The wāw is circumstantial, with an implied "We"; the clause نعلم is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as an implied ḥāl. You may make the wāw resumptive, in which case the sentence is resumptive. ما is a direct object, and the clause توسوس is the ṣila. You may make ما a maṣdar, the implied form being "and We know the whispering of his soul to him". به is attached to توسوس and نفسه is the agent. ونحن: the wāw is a conjunction; نحن is the mubtadaʾ; أقرب is the khabar; إليه is attached to أقرب, and من حبل الوريد is also attached to أقرب.
(إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى الْمُتَلَقِّيانِ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ قَعِيدٌ): إذ may be an adverbial for أقرب, or the implied form may be "remember". The clause يتلقى is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. المتلقيان is the agent; عن اليمين is an advanced khabar; الشمال is conjoined to اليمين; قعيد is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of المتلقيان.
(ما يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ): ما is negative; يلفظ is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to the human being; من is a redundant preposition; قول is genitive in form, accusative in position as the direct object of يلفظ; إلا is a particle of restriction; لديه is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted advanced khabar; رقيب عتيد is a delayed mubtadaʾ, which is singular in form and in meaning "two watchers, present", or "two angels described as watchers, present". It is also said that there is no need for this implied form, but it is preferable to make the two descriptions for one thing, i.e. "except that with him is an angel described as a watcher, present", meaning a guardian, in attendance.
(وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذلِكَ ما كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ): A resumptive discourse, brought in to explain what they will meet of death and resurrection and the terrors that follow them. جاءت سكرة الموت is verb and agent; بالحق is a ḥāl, i.e. "while it is accompanied by the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment. It is also said to be for transitivity, meaning "and the stupor of death brought the reality of the matter, which Allah gave utterance to in His books and sent with His messengers". Al-Zamakhsharī preferred this reading. ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; ما is the khabar; كان with its ism; منه is attached to تحيد; the clause تحيد is the khabar of كنت; the clause كنت is the ṣila of ما; and the clause ذلك ما كنت is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "and it is said to him at the time of death: this is that matter you now see, not that from which you used to shy away in your life, so flight did not benefit you and escape did not save you".
(وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْوَعِيدِ): Conjoined to وجاءت سكرة الموت. نفخ is a passive past verb; في الصور is attached to نفخ; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ and يوم الوعيد its khabar; and the pointing is to the verbal noun of نفخ.

dervis-irab:21-30.t:
* I'rab:
(وَجاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَها سائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ): The wāw is a conjunction; جاءت كل نفس is verb and agent; معها is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted advanced khabar; سائق is a delayed mubtadaʾ; شهيد is conjoined to سائق; and the nominal sentence is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of كل, or in the position of the accusative as an adjective of نفس, i.e. "with it is one who drives it and bears witness against it". You may also make it circumstantial.
(لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ): The sentence is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "it is said to every soul". The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; كان with its ism; في غفلة is its khabar; من هذا is attached to غفلة. The fāʾ is a conjunction; كشفنا is verb and agent; عنك is attached to كشفنا; غطاءك is the direct object. The fāʾ is a conjunction; بصرك is the mubtadaʾ; اليوم is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; حديد is the khabar of بصرك.
(وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ هذا ما لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ): The wāw is a conjunction; قال قرينه is verb and agent. What is meant by the qarīn (companion) is the angel appointed over him, or the devil who made evil seem attractive to him. هذا is the mubtadaʾ. ما may be an indefinite noun described, with عتيد as its adjective, and لدي an adverbial attached to عتيد, i.e. "this is a thing present with me", meaning "in attendance with me". On this view لدي may be a description of ما and عتيد a second description, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is present". ما may also be a relative noun meaning "that which", with لدي its ṣila and عتيد the khabar of the relative; the relative with its ṣila being the khabar of the demonstrative. ما may also be a substitute for هذا, as a relative or as an indefinite noun described by لدي, with عتيد the khabar of هذا. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed for عتيد that it be a substitute, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. The text of al-Zamakhsharī's i'rab follows. He said: «If you ask: how is this speech parsed? I say: if you make ما an indefinite noun described, then عتيد is an adjective of it; and if you make it a relative, then it is a substitute, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.» Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «His words, Exalted is He, هذا is a mubtadaʾ, and in ما there are two aspects. One is that it is indefinite and عتيد is its adjective, and لدي is governed by عتيد; it is also possible that لدي be an adjective too, attached to an omitted word, and ما with its adjective is the khabar of هذا. The second is that ما means "that which"; on this ما is a mubtadaʾ, لدي is the ṣila, عتيد is the khabar of ما, and the clause is the khabar of هذا. It is also possible that ما be a substitute for هذا. It is also possible that عتيد be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and ما لدي be the khabar of هذا, i.e. "it is present". Had this occurred outside the Qur'an, its being in the accusative as a ḥāl would be permissible.»
(أَلْقِيا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ): The sentence is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "it is said: cast". ألقيا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn because of its attachment to the alif of the dual. It is said that He addressed the two angels, the driver and the witness; and it is said that the address is to one person, and the speech was put in the form of an address to two, because it is the custom of the Arabs to apply an address to two to one or to many. An example is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل ... بسقط اللوى بين الدخول فحومل
(Stop, you two, let us weep at the memory of a beloved and an abode, at the edge of the sand-dune between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal.)
And the saying of another:
فإن تزجراني يا ابن عفان أنزجر ... وإن ترعياني أحم عرضا ممنعا
(If you two rebuke me, O son of ʿAffān, I shall be restrained; and if you two guard me, I shall protect an inviolable honour.)
He addressed one as one addresses two. The Arabs did so only because a man's fewest helpers are two: the herder of his camels and the herder of his sheep; and likewise the minimum of a company is three. So the address to two came to be applied to one, because their tongues had passed over it. It is also possible that what is meant is "cast, cast" and "stop, stop"; so the attaching of the alif is a sign indicating that what is meant is the repetition of the word, as Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī said concerning His words, Exalted is He, «رب ارجعون», of which the meaning is "return me, return me, return me": the wāw was made a sign signalling that the meaning is repetition of the word several times. It is also said that he meant ألقين (with emphatic nūn), and Imruʾ al-Qays meant فقن (emphatic nūn) for emphasis, so the nūn was turned into alif in continuous speech, because this nūn is also turned in pause, and continuous speech was carried over onto pause. Do you not see that if you paused at His words «لنسفعن» you would say لنسفعا? From this is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
وصلّ على حين العشيات والضحى ... ولا تحمد الشيطان والله فاحمدا
(And pray at the times of the evenings and the forenoon, and do not praise Satan, but praise Allah.) He meant فاحمدن, and turned the emphatic nūn into alif. في جهنم is attached to ألقيا; كل كفار is the direct object; عنيد is an adjective of كفار.
(مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُرِيبٍ): successive adjectives.
(الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ فَأَلْقِياهُ فِي الْعَذابِ الشَّدِيدِ): الذي may be a substitute for كل, in which case it is in the position of the accusative; or a substitute for كفار, in which case it is in the position of the genitive; it may be accusative for censure; or it may be a mubtadaʾ, in which case it is in the position of the nominative. The clause جعل is the ṣila; مع الله is an adverbial attached to an omitted second direct object; إلها آخر is the first direct object. The fāʾ is a connective, because the relative resembles a condition in generality. ألقياه is an imperative verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is the khabar of الذي if it is made a khabar; the first view is preferable. في العذاب is attached to ألقياه and الشديد is an adjective of العذاب.
(قالَ قَرِينُهُ رَبَّنا ما أَطْغَيْتُهُ وَلكِنْ كانَ فِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ): قال قرينه is verb and agent; ربنا is a vocative, a muḍāf; ما is negative; أطغيته is verb, agent and direct object; ولكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative because it was lightened; كان is a defective past verb whose ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; في ضلال is attached to an omitted khabar of كان; بعيد is an adjective of ضلال. The clause قال قرينه is resumptive, and for that reason it came without a wāw. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: why was this sentence left without the wāw while it was brought into the first? I say: because it was begun anew as the sentences occurring in the report of a dialogue are begun anew, as you have seen in the report of the dialogue between Moses and Pharaoh. If you ask: where is the dialogue here? I say: when his companion said "This is what is with me, present", followed by His saying "Our Lord, I did not make him rebel", followed by "Do not dispute before Me", it is known that there was a speech from the disbeliever, but it was dropped because of what indicates it, as though he had said: "Lord, he led me to rebel", so his companion said: "Our Lord, I did not make him rebel". As for the first sentence, its conjunction was necessary, to indicate the joining of its meaning and that of what precedes it in occurrence, I mean the coming of every soul with the two angels and the saying of his companion what he said to him.»
(قالَ لا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِالْوَعِيدِ): لا is prohibitive; تختصموا is an imperfect verb, jussive, and the clause is the content of the saying; لدي is an adverbial attached to تختصموا; the wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of certainty; قدمت is verb and agent; إليكم is attached to قدمت. The bāʾ in بالوعيد is redundant, like it is in «ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة», or transitive, on the view that qaddama is the reflexive form with the meaning taqaddama. It is also possible that the verb falls upon the sentence of His words «ما يبدل القول لدي وما أنا بظلّام للعبيد», with بالوعيد a ḥāl, i.e. "I put this forward to you accompanied by the threat, joined with it", or "I put it forward to you as a warning to you of it".
(ما يُبَدَّلُ الْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وَما أَنَا بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ): ما is negative; يبدل is a passive imperfect verb; القول is the nāʾib fāʿil; لدي is an adverbial attached to يبدل; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is a negative in the Ḥijāzī manner; أنا is its ism; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; ظلام is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما; and للعبيد is attached to ظلام.
(يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ): For its governor there are two aspects: you may make it accusative by an implied "remember", or attach it to ظلام, for if He wrongs not on this day, the negation of wrong from Him on other days is more fitting. The clause نقول لجهنم is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause هل امتلأت is the content of the saying; وتقول is conjoined to نقول; هل is an interrogative particle; من is a redundant preposition; مزيد is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "existing".

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «فكشفنا عنك غطاءك» there is a kināya (metonymy) for heedlessness, as though it covered all of him or his eyes, so that he cannot see. When the Resurrection comes, heedlessness leaves him, realities are uncovered to him, and the rust that was drawn over him before clears away, so he sees what he did not see in his life. It is also possible that the "covering" is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), with heedlessness made like a covering that covers his whole body, or a film that covers his eyes, so that he sees nothing.
2- The metaphor with the likened term implied (istiʿāra makniyya): it is possible to take His words, Exalted is He, «يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت وتقول هل من مزيد» as an implied metaphor of imaginative representation (takhyīliyya). The Muʿtazila took this course, as did those of the Ahl al-Sunna who agreed with them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The questioning of Hell and its reply belong to the category of takhyīl, by which it is intended to depict the meaning in the heart and fix it. In it are two meanings. One is that it will be filled, despite its vastness and the remoteness of its edges, until nothing more can be contained in it and nothing can be added to its fullness, because of His words, Exalted is He, «لأملأنّ جهنم». The second is that it is so vast that those who enter it enter, and there is still room in it for more. It is possible that "Is there any more?" is a deeming-numerous of those entering it, or a request for increase out of rage at the disobedient. And al-mazīd is either a maṣdar, like al-maḥīd and al-maḥīd, or a passive participle, like al-mabīʿ.» It is also possible to take it literally. The majority of the Ahl al-Sunna proceeded on the literal view and rejected al-Zamakhsharī's and others' use of the term takhyīl, saying it is objectionable in wording and in meaning. As to wording, it is among the expressions that give a wrong impression in respect of the majesty of Allah, Exalted is He, even if their meanings are sound, and what impression is stronger than that of the word takhyīl? Do you not see how Allah used it for what He reported to be sorcery and falsehood, in His words «يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى»? There is no doubt about the necessity of avoiding it. As to meaning, the Ahl al-Sunna believe that the questioning of Hell and its reply are real, and that Allah, Exalted is He, creates in it perception of that, on its condition. Furthermore, poets clung to the hems of this lofty eloquence. The first to glance at its sky was al-Farazdaq, when he said of Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib in his ode that begins:
هذا الذي تعرف البطحاء وطأته ... والبيت يعرفه والحلّ والحرم
(This is the one whose footstep the valley of Mecca knows, whom the House knows, and the unconsecrated land and the sanctuary.)
He said:
يكاد يمسكه عرفان راحته ... ركن الحطيم إذا ما جاء يستلم
(The corner of the Ḥaṭīm almost holds him, in recognition of his palm, when he comes to touch it.)
Abū Tammām followed him:
لو يعلم الركن من قد جاء يلثمه ... لخرّ يلثم منه موطئ القدم
(If the Corner knew who had come to kiss it, it would fall down to kiss the place where his foot treads.)
Al-Buḥturī took it and did well:
فلو أن مشتاقا تكلف فوق ما ... في سعة لسعى إليك المنبر
(If one longing had taken on more than is within his capacity, the pulpit would have run to you.)
And al-Mutanabbī followed this path with his words:
لو تعقل الشجر التي قابلتها ... مدّت محيّية إليك الأغصنا
(If the trees you faced had understanding, they would have stretched out their branches to you in greeting.)
In the Jāhiliyya this meaning had already occurred in the saying of ʿAntara describing his horse in his Muʿallaqa:
فازور من وقع القنا بلبانه ... وشكا إليّ بعبرة وتحمحم
(It veered away from the blows of the spears with its chest, and complained to me with tears and neighing.)
Do not miss the beauty of the sensory imagination and the embodiment, in this metaphor, of Hell, raging and insatiably greedy, upon which fall in crowds those who in their worldly life used to stop their ears against the call to guidance, and persisted in their error and obstinacy; and here they are now answering its call, compelled.

dervis-irab:31-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَأُزْلِفَتِ): and was brought near. You say azlafahu: he brought him near; azlafa al-ashyāʾ: he gathered them; azlafa al-dalīl al-qawm: the guide made the people advance; and he drove them on stage after stage (muzlifa baʿda muzlifa), i.e. a stage after a stage.
(مَحِيصٍ): a place to turn aside to. In al-Qāmūs: «ḥāṣa ʿanhu yaḥīṣu ḥayṣan wa-ḥayṣatan wa-ḥuyūṣan wa-maḥīṣan wa-maḥāṣan wa-ḥayaṣānan: he turned aside and swerved, like inḥāṣa; or it is said, of allies, "ḥāṣū", and of enemies, "they were routed". Al-maḥīṣ is the place of swerving, of turning aside, of inclining, of fleeing. A ḥayyūṣ beast is a shying one. Al-ḥayṣāʾ is the narrow one of modesty.» And under the root b-y-ṣ he said: «He fell into ḥayṣ bayṣ, and ḥiyaṣ biyaṣ, and ḥayṣ bayṣ ... with fatḥa on the first and last of them, with kasra on both, and with fatḥa on the first and kasra on the last; and they may be inflected in the second; and in ḥāṣa bāṣa, that is a confusion from which there is no escape. You made the earth ḥayṣ bayṣ for him and ḥayṣan bayṣan: you constrained him until he could not move about in it.» Ḥayṣ Bayṣ is the nickname of the Tamīmī poet Shihāb al-Dīn; ḥayṣa bayṣa were two words narrated from him in describing the crowding of the people, and they prevailed over his name and he was nicknamed by them. He has poetry in description, satire and praise; his language is pure Arabic. He died in Baghdad in the year 1179 CE.

* I'rab:
(وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ): The wāw is a conjunction; أزلفت is a passive past verb; الجنة is the nāʾib fāʿil; للمتقين is attached to أزلفت; غير بعيد is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), because it stands in the place of the adverbial, being its adjective, i.e. "a place not far". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative as a ḥāl. He said: «Its being masculine is because it is on the pattern of a maṣdar, like al-zaʾīr and al-ṣalīl; and for maṣdars the masculine and feminine are equal when used as description; or it is on the omission of the described noun, i.e. "a thing not far".»
(هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ): هذا is the mubtadaʾ; ما is its khabar; the clause توعدون is the ṣila; ولكل, preposition and genitive noun, is a substitute for His words للمتقين by repetition of the preposition; and the clause هذا ما توعدون is parenthetical, a separation between the substitute and what it substitutes for.
(مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ): من is a substitute for كل, after كل itself is a substitute for المتقين, except that it is a substitute for المتقين as well, since repetition of the substitute with the substituted-for being one is not allowed. It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who feared", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ادخلوها بسلام as will come, because من has the sense of plural. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a vocative, like their saying "من لا يزال محسنا أحسن إلي", with the vocative particle omitted for the sake of nearness. The clause خشي الرحمن is the ṣila; بالغيب is a ḥāl of the direct object, i.e. "he feared Him while He was absent, unseen, not known to him".
(ادْخُلُوها بِسَلامٍ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ): The sentence is the content of an omitted saying as preceded. ادخلوها is verb, agent and direct object; بسلام is a ḥāl of the agent, i.e. "safe from every fearful thing", so it is a concurrent ḥāl; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; يوم الخلود is the khabar.
(لَهُمْ ما يَشاؤُنَ فِيها وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ): لهم is an advanced khabar; ما is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يشاءون is the ṣila; فيها is a ḥāl of the relative, or attached to يشاءون; لدينا is an adverbial attached to an omitted advanced khabar; مزيد is a delayed mubtadaʾ.
(وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ هَلْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): The wāw is resumptive, and the discourse is resumptive, brought to mention the destruction of past generations. كم is the declarative kam (khabariyya), accusative by what follows it as a direct object; أهلكنا is verb and agent; قبلهم is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; من قرن is the tamyīz of the declarative كم; هم is the mubtadaʾ; أشد the khabar; the clause is an adjective of كم or of its tamyīz; منهم is attached to أشد; بطشا is a tamyīz. فنقبوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; نقبوا is verb and agent; the conjunction is on the sense, as though "their might was intense, so they roamed"; في البلاد is attached to نقبوا. هل is an interrogative particle; من is a redundant preposition; محيص is genitive in form, nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "for them or for others". The clause هل من محيص is the content of an omitted saying, and the clause of saying is a ḥāl of the wāw of نقبوا, i.e. "so they roamed the lands saying: is there any place of escape?".
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ): إن is a particle that resembles a verb; في ذلك is the advanced khabar of إن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; ذكرى is the ism of إن; لمن is attached to an omitted adjective of ذكرى; the clause كان is the ṣila; له is the advanced khabar of كان and قلب its delayed ism; أو is a conjunction; ألقى السمع is verb, a latent agent, and direct object; the wāw is circumstantial; هو is the mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «لمن خشي الرحمن بالغيب»: how can fear be joined with the name al-Raḥmān, which indicates the vastness of mercy? The answer is that in this there is intensification of praise for the one who fears, because if he fears Him while knowing the vastness of His mercy, then consider his fear, after which there is no fear; just as He praised him for fear even though the one feared is absent (unseen).

dervis-irab:38-45.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لُغُوبٍ): fatigue. In al-Mukhtār: «al-lughūb (with two ḍammas) is fatigue and exhaustion, of the pattern dakhala; and laghiba (with kasra), lughūban, is a weak dialect.» In al-Miṣbāḥ it is of the pattern qatala, and in al-Qāmūs it is of the pattern manaʿa, and also karuma.
(أَدْبارَ): with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of dubur (with two ḍammas). It was read with kasra on the hamza (idbār), as a maṣdar standing in the place of an adverb of time; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamza read it so. A group of the Companions and Successors said: idbār al-sujūd is the two rakʿas after the Maghrib, and idbār al-nujūm is the two rakʿas before the dawn.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَما مَسَّنا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ): The wāw is resumptive, and the discourse is resumptive, brought to refute the Jews who said that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rested and lay on His back upon the Throne on the Sabbath, and so they left work on it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; خلقنا is verb and agent; السموات is the direct object; الأرض is conjoined to السموات; في ستة أيام is attached to خلقنا. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; ما is negative; مسنا is a past verb, and نا is the direct object; من is a redundant preposition; لغوب is genitive in form, nominative in position, because it is the agent.
(فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; اصبر is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; على ما يقولون is attached to اصبر; سبح is an imperative verb; بحمد ربك is a ḥāl of the agent of سبح, i.e. "pray, praising"; قبل طلوع الشمس is an adverbial attached to سبح; and قبل الغروب is conjoined to the adverbial.
(وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ): The wāw is a conjunction; من الليل is attached to سبح; the fāʾ is a conjunction; سبحه is an imperative verb, a latent agent, and the hāʾ is the direct object; أدبار السجود is an adverbial.
(وَاسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ): Conjoined to what precedes. استمع is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; its object is omitted, i.e. "and listen to the call of the caller"; the adverbial is attached to استمع. It is said that the implied object is "what I say to you"; on this, يوم is accusative by an implied "they will come out", indicated by His words «ذلك يوم الخروج». The yāʾ of ينادي was dropped to follow the written form, and المناد is the agent (the yāʾ being dropped in some readings, also following the written form); من مكان is attached to ينادي and قريب is an adjective. The caller is Isrāfīl; it is also said that it is Jibrīl and the blower is Isrāfīl, and al-Shihāb al-Khafājī preferred this.
(يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ): The adverbial is a substitute for the first adverbial; the clause يسمعون is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of "when" to it; الصيحة is the direct object; بالحق is a ḥāl of the wāw in يسمعون or of الصيحة; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ and يوم الخروج the khabar.
(إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ): إن with its ism; نحن is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; the clause نحيي is the khabar of إنا or the khabar of نحن, with the sentence being the khabar of إن; إلينا is an advanced khabar and المصير a delayed mubtadaʾ.
(يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِراعاً ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنا يَسِيرٌ): The adverbial is a substitute for what precedes, though some prevented that because of the multiplicity, and attached it to المصير. The clause تشقق is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. The origin of تشقق is تتشقق, and it was read with shadda on the shīn by assimilation of the second tāʾ into it. الأرض is the agent; عنهم is attached to تشقق; سراعا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in عنهم; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ and حشر the khabar; علينا is attached to يسير; and يسير is the khabar of ذلك.
(نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ): نحن is the mubtadaʾ; أعلم is the khabar; بما is attached to أعلم, and ما is a relative or a maṣdar. The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative in the Ḥijāzī manner; أنت is its ism; عليهم is attached to جبار; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and جبار is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما.
(فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; ذكر is an imperative verb; بالقرآن is attached to ذكر; من is the direct object; the clause يخاف is the ṣila; وعيد is the object of يخاف; and the yāʾ of the first person was dropped to follow the written form.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾.
Qāf: in it is the meaning by which He swore [181/b]. It is reported that it means "it has been decreed (quḍiya), by Allah", as is said of ḥumma: "it has been decreed, by Allah"; "ḥumma, by Allah" means: it has been decreed.
And it is said that (Qāf) is a mountain surrounding the earth. If it is so, it is as though it is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "it is Qāf, by Allah"; and it [should] have shown its nominative ending, because it would be a noun and not a spelled letter. Perhaps the qāf alone was mentioned from its name, as the poet said:
قلنا لها: قفى، فقالت: قافْ
(We said to her: "Stop!" and she said: "Qāf.")
She mentioned the qāf, meaning the qāf of wuqūf (stopping), i.e. "I am stopping."

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً﴾.
Speech before which there appears nothing to which this would be an answer; but its meaning is implied. It was only, and Allah knows best: ﴿ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ﴾ "you will surely be raised" after death. So they said: "Shall we be raised when we have become dust?", denying the resurrection; then they said: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾, denying it altogether. [And] His saying (بعيد) is as you say to a man who errs in a question: "You have gone a way far from the right", i.e. you have erred.

farraa:4-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾: what it consumes of them.
His saying: ﴿فِيۤ أَمْرٍ مَّرِيجٍ﴾.
In error.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍ﴾.
There is no gap or crack in it.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ﴾.
The grain is the harvested; and it is among what is annexed to itself, like His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَذا لَهُو حَقُّ الْيَقِين﴾; and like it: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ﴾.
The ḥabl (rope) is the warīd (jugular vein) itself, annexed to itself because the wording of its two names differs. Al-warīd is a vein between the throat and the two neck-tendons (ʿilbāwān).

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ﴾.
Tall. One says: "it has grown (basaqa) in height"; so they are the tall palms.
His saying: ﴿لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ﴾.
He means: the palm spathe (kufurrā) while it is in its sheaths, it is naḍīd, i.e. arranged one part over another; when it comes out of its sheaths it is not naḍīd.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلأَوَّلِ﴾.
He says: how, in their view, should We be wearied by the resurrection when We were not wearied by creating them the first time? Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. they are in error and doubt.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾.
The hāʾ is for ما; and in ما توسوس you may make the hāʾ for the man whom it whispers to, meaning: it whispers to him and talks to him.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾.
It says قعيد and does not say قعيدان (dual). Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "seated (qaʿīd) on the right and on the left" means seated ones (quʿūd); so he made qaʿīd a plural, as you make al-rasūl (messenger) for a group and for two. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِين﴾, of Moses and his brother. And the poet said:
ألِكْنى إليها، وخيرُ الرسو * لِ أعلَمُهم بنواحِى الْخَبَرْ
(Be my messenger to her; and the best of messengers is the one most knowing of the sides of the news.)
So he made al-rasūl for the plural. This is one view. And if you wish, you make al-qaʿīd singular, one being sufficient for its companion, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بما عِندنا، وأنت بما * عندك راضٍ، والرأىُ مختلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content [rāḍin, singular]; and opinion differs.)
And like it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إِنِّى ضَمِنت لمن أتانى ما جَنَى * وأبَى، وَكان وكنت غير غَدُورِ
(I guaranteed to whoever came to me [protection from] what he had committed, and my father [did likewise]; and he was, and I was, not treacherous [ghadūr, singular].)
And he did not say غدورين (dual).

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: سكرة الحق بالموت.
