If you wish, you mean by (بالحق) that He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if you wish, you make the stupor (al-sakra) the death itself, annexed to itself, as though you said: "the true stupor came with death". And His saying: ﴿سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾: he says: with the truth which had not been clear to them of the matter of the Hereafter. And the truth may be the death, i.e. the stupor of death came with the reality of death.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾.
He says: you used to deny, but today you are knowing, of piercing sight; and sight here is knowledge, not with the eye.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾.
You put عتيد in the nominative by making it a predicate whose ṣila (relative clause) belongs to ما; and if you wish, you make it resumptive (mustaʾnaf), like His saying: ﴿هَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخٌ﴾. Had it been accusative, it would have been correct, because هذا and ما are both definite, so العتيد is detached (yuqṭaʿ) from them [as a ḥāl].

farraa:24-24.t:
[182/a] His saying: ﴿أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾.
The Arabs command the one and the group with what two are commanded, saying to a man: "Get up (قوما, dual) away from us". I heard one of them [say]: "Woe to you! Saddle her (ارحلاها, dual) and drive her (ازجرها, singular)". And one of them recited to me:
فقلت لصاحبى لا تحبسانا * بنزع أصوله، واجتزَّ شيحا
(I said to my companion: "Do not detain us [dual] by pulling up its roots, and cut [singular] some wormwood.")
He said: and it is also transmitted: واجدزّ, meaning واجتز. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
وإن تزجرانى يا ابن عفان أنزجر * وإن تدعانى أَحْمِ عرضاً ممنَّعاً
(If you two [i.e. you] restrain me, O son of ʿAffān, I am restrained; and if you two leave me, I will defend an honour that is well guarded.)
We think this comes from them because the fewest helpers a man has with his camels and sheep are two; and likewise a travelling company, the fewest they are is three; so the speech to one ran as speech to his two companions. Do you not see that the poets most often say: "O my two companions, O my two friends"? Imruʾ al-Qays said:
خليلىّ، مرّا بِى على أم جندب * نُقضِّى لُبانات الفؤاد المعذب
(My two friends, pass with me by Umm Jundab, that we may fulfil the needs of the tormented heart.)
Then he said:
ألَمْ تَرَ أنى كلما جئت طارقا * وجدت بها طيبا وإن لم تطيب
(Have you [singular] not seen that whenever I came by night, I found fragrance with her, even when she was not perfumed?)
So he said ألم تر, returning to the singular, while the beginning of his speech was to two. He said: and another recited to me:
خليلىّ قوما فى عَطالة فانظرا * أناراً ترى من نحو بابَيْن أو برقا
(My two friends, stand on ʿAṭāla and look: do you [singular] see a fire towards Bābayn, or lightning?)
And some of them [recite]: أنارا نرى.
His saying: ﴿مَا أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾: the angel who used to write down the evil deeds of the unbeliever says it. That is because the unbeliever said: "He used to hurry me away from repentance"; so he said: "I did not make him transgress, O Lord, but he was astray."

farraa:29-29.t: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ﴾, i.e. no lie is told before Me, because of His knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, of the unseen of that.

farraa:32-33.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ﴾ ﴿مَّنْ خَشِيَ﴾.
If you wish, you make (مَن) genitive, following His saying (لكلّ); and if you wish, you make it resumptive, so it is nominative, with the conditional (jazāʾ) meaning intended: whoever fears the All-Merciful in the unseen, it will be said to him: "Enter Paradise". And (ادْخُلوها) is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition, before which you have implied the verb of saying, and you made it a verb for the plural because مَن may have the sense of the plural.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾.
The reading of the readers. He says: they pierced through the lands and travelled in them; so was there for them any escape from death? You imply كان here, as He said: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِّنْ قَرْيَةٍ هي أَشَدُّ قُوّةً مِّنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتى أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ فَلا نَاصِرَ لَهُم﴾, and the meaning is: they had no helper when they were destroyed. And whoever reads: (فَنقِّبوا) فى البلاد, with kasra on the qāf, it is like a threat, i.e. go about in the lands, come and go.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾.
He says: for whoever has intellect. This is allowed in Arabic: you say "You have no heart", "Your heart is not with you" and "Where has your heart gone?", meaning the intellect in all of that.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾.
He says: or he lends his hearing to the Book of Allah while he is shahīd, i.e. present, not absent.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾.
He says: of weariness. That is because the Jews of the people of Medina said: He began the creation of the heavens and the earth on Sunday and finished on Friday, and rested on the Sabbath. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾, belying their saying. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it: من لَغوب, with fatḥa on the lām, and it is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ ٱلسُّجُودِ﴾.
And إِدبار. Whoever reads وأدبار makes it the plural of dubur: adbār; and they are the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer. That came from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: [182/b] "وأدبار السجود: the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer"; and ﴿وإِدْبارَ النُّجومِ﴾: the two rakʿas (before the dawn prayer). ʿĀṣim used to give fatḥa to the one in Qāf and kasra to the one in al-Ṭūr; giving both kasra and giving both fatḥa are allowed.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.
It is said that Gabriel, peace be upon him, will come to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and call out for the Gathering; that is His saying: ﴿مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعاً﴾.
To the place of Gathering; and تُشَقق [is also read]; and the meaning is one, like "the man died (māta)" and "was caused to die (umīta)".

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾.
He says: you are not a dominator over them. He put al-jabbār in the position of al-sulṭān (the ruler), from al-jabriyya (compulsion). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
ويوم الحَزن إذ حشَدَت مَعدٌّ * وكان الناسُ إلا نحن دينا عصينا عزمةَ الجبار حتى * صبحنا الجوفَ ألفا مُعْلمينا
(And the Day of al-Ḥazn, when Maʿadd gathered and all people but us were in subjection: we defied the resolve of the jabbār until we came upon al-Jawf in the morning, a thousand men wearing battle-marks.)
By al-jabbār he meant al-Mundhir, because of his rule.
And al-Kalbī said, with his isnad: لستَ عَلَيْهِمْ بجَبّار: he says: you were not sent to compel (tajburahum) them to Islam and guidance; you were sent only as a reminder, so remind. That was before he was commanded to fight them.
The Arabs do not say faʿʿāl from afʿaltu: they do not say "this is a kharrāj" or "a dakhkhāl", meaning mudkhil and mukhrij, from adkhaltu and akhrajtu; they say only dakhkhāl from dakhaltu, and faʿʿāl from faʿaltu. The Arabs have said darrāk from adraktu, but it is anomalous. If you take al-jabbār in this sense [i.e. from ajbara], it is a valid view.
And I have heard some of the Arabs say: "jabarahu ʿalā al-amr", meaning ajbarahu (he compelled him); so al-jabbār from this dialect is sound, meaning: one who subdues them and compels them.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «والقرآن»: sworn by (muqsam bihi), genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "I swear".

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from «أن» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "at the coming"; the preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «منذر»; the clause «فقال الكافرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «عجبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted apodosis (jawāb) "we will return". The conditional clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «ذلك رجع» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «قد علمنا» is resumptive; the preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تَنْقُص»; the clause «وعندنا كتاب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «كذَّبوا» is resumptive; the conditional clause is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; the clause «فهم في أمر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كَذَّبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «أفلم ينظروا» is resumptive; the clause «كيف بنيناها» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «السماء»; the adverb «فوقهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماء». «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl from the pronoun hāʾ. The clause «وما لها من فروج» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «بنيناها»; «ما» is negative, «فروج» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The wāw is resumptive; «الأرض» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «مَدَدْناها» is explicative. The clause «وألقينا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied "We spread"; the preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted object of «أنبتنا», i.e. "We caused to grow plants being of every …".

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «تبصرة»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «لكل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «نزلنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «مددنا» implied in verse (7).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «النخل» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «حب»; «باسقات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause «لها طلع» is a second ḥāl from «النخل».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «رزقا»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «للعباد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رزقا». The clause «أحيينا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أنبتنا» in verse (9). The clause «كذلك الخروج» is resumptive, and the preposition «كذلك» is attached to the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «كلٌ كذب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from those previously mentioned; the clause «فحقَّ وعيد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كل كذب»; «وعيد» is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «أفعيينا» is resumptive; the clause «بل هم في لبس» is resumptive; the preposition «من خلق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «لَبْس».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The wāw is resumptive; the clause «نعلم» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and We know", and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «ونحن أقرب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «ونحن نعلم», and the two prepositions «إليه» and «من حبل» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقرب».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَقْرَبُ}; the preposition «عن اليمين» is attached to a khabar (predicate) placed first for the mubtadaʾ (subject) «قعيد», and the clause «عن اليمين ... قعيد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المتلقيان».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «ما يلفظ» is resumptive; «قول» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «لديه رقيب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يلفظ».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «وجاءت» is resumptive; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سكرة»; the clause «ذلك ما كنت» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied, resumptive saying, i.e. "and it will be said to him at that time".

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (ونفخ في الصور) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive, and the preposition is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause «ذلك يوم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وجاءت كل نفس» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ}, and the clause «معها سائق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كل نفس».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «لقد كنت» occurs as the answer to the oath; the clause «فكشفنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كنت»; the clause «فبصرك اليوم حديد» is conjoined to the clause «كشفنا»; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «حديد».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «هذا»: mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is «عتيد». «ما» is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from «ذا»; «لديّ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «منَّاع» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {كَفَّارٍ}; «للخير» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «منَّاع», and the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «الذي» is a badal (substitute) from {كُلَّ} in verse (24); «مع» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, a second object; and the clause «فألقياه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أَلْقِيَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «قال قرينه» is resumptive; the clause «ولكن كان» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «ما أطغيته».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «قال» is resumptive; the clause «وقد قَدَّمْتُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the two prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قَدَّمْتُ».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «ما يبدَّل» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «وما أنا بظلام» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like «ليس»; «العبيد» is the object of «ظلام», and the lām is redundant, for strengthening.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ظلام»; the clause «وتقول» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «نقول»; «مزيد» is mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "there".

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «وأزلفت» is resumptive; «غير» is an adverb of place, the original being "at a place not far".

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «ما» is a relative, the khabar (predicate) of «هذا»; the clause «هذا ما توعدون» is parenthetical between the badal (substitute) «لكل أواب» and the noun it replaces, {لِلْمُتَّقِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «من» is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from «كل أواب»; the preposition «بالغيب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خشي»; and the preposition «بقلب» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «جاء».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «ادخلوها» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied, resumptive saying; the preposition «بسلام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ادخلوها»; the clause «ذلك يوم» is parenthetical between the ḥāl and the one it describes.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «لهم ما يشاءون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {ادْخُلُوهَا}, and the clause «ولدينا مزيد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لهم ما يشاءون».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «وكم أهلكنا» is resumptive; «كم» is the declarative (khabariyya) one, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «من قرن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم»; the clause «هم أشد» is a naʿt of «قرن»; the preposition «منهم» is attached to «أشد»; «بطشا» is a tamyīz (specification). The clause «فنقَّبوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «هم أشد». The clause «هل من محيص» is resumptive; «محيص» is mubtadaʾ (subject), «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "there".

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The lām in «لذكرى» is for emphasis; the preposition «لمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرى»; and the clause «وهو شهيد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الأرض»; the clause «وما مسَّنا من لغوب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «لغوب» is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive; the preposition «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «سبِّح».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The wāw is conjunctive; «من الليل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبِّحه», and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); «وأدبار» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the position of «من الليل», which is the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «واستمع» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «سبح»; the object of «استمع» is omitted, i.e. "listen to the call of the caller", and «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «استمع», i.e. "listen to that on a day". His words «يناد»: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is omitted in writing following its omission in pronunciation.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَ يُنَادِ}; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصيحة».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «نحن» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun «نا»; the clause «نحيي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; the clause «وإلينا المصير» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «نميت».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {الْمَصِيرُ}; «سراعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عنهم»; the preposition «علينا» is attached to «يسير».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم»; the clause «وما أنت عليهم بجبار» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «نحن أعلم», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما». The clause «فذكِّر» is resumptive, and «وعيد» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, وَالْقُرآن: an oath. Its apodosis (answer), according to al-Akhfash, is قد علمنا, with omission of the lām, i.e. "We have certainly known" (لقد علمنا). Al-Zajjāj said the answer is omitted, its implied form being "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be resurrected" (والقرآن المجيد لنبعثن), because they denied the resurrection in the verse after it. It is also said that what comes before the oath stands in place of the answer, and that the meaning of ق is "the matter has been decreed" — "By the glorious Qur'an, the matter has been decreed" — so "the matter has been decreed" is the answer, and ق indicated it. It is also said that ق is the name of the mountain, so its implied form is "it is Qāf" (هو ق), and والقرآن المجيد; and the clause stands in place of the answer to the oath.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying أئذا متْنا: the governing word in إذا is an omitted verb indicated by the speech, because they were people who denied the resurrection, so it is as if they said "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" (أنبعث إذا متنا). متنا does not govern it, because إذا is annexed to متنا, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying وَحب الحصيد: according to the Kufans this is the annexation of a thing to itself; its implied form according to them is "and the harvested grain" (والحب الحصيد), i.e. the reaped; then the alif and lām were omitted from الحب and it was annexed to الحصيد, which is its naʿt (adjective), and the naʿt is the thing described. According to the Basrans it is a genuine annexation, but it contains the omission of the thing described and the setting up of the adjective in its place; its implied form is "and the grain of the harvested plant" (وحب النبت الحصيد), i.e. the reaped; so النبت was omitted and its adjective set up in its place, and الحب was annexed to الحصيد on this assumption.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying رزقا للعباد: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it is also said: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying {إِن كل إِلَّا كذب الرُّسُل}: إنْ means ما (not); كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and إلا with what follows it is the khabar (predicate). كل means "all of them" (كلهم). Sībawayh related مررت بكلٍّ جالسا ("I passed by all of them sitting"), putting جالسا in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because كل is definite, since its implied form is كلهم. For that reason some grammarians permitted كلُّ منطلق, making كل indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because of the omission of what it is annexed to, treating it like قبل and بعد.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying توسوس بِهِ: the هاء refers back to ما; it is also said: to الإنسان. And the بـ is in place of إلى.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {عَن الْيَمين وَعَن الشمَال قعيد}: the doctrine of Sībawayh is that a قعيد has been omitted from the first part of the speech because the second indicates it. The doctrine of al-Mubarrad is that the قعيد which is in the recitation belongs to the first, but was postponed for latitude of expression, and قعيد was omitted from the second because the first indicates it. The doctrine of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ is that the قعيد which is in the recitation stands for two and more, and there is no omission in the speech.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying مَعهَا سائق: [سائق is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and معها the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of نفس or of كل. [Translator's note: the edition reads «accusative» (نصب); since نفس and كل are genitive in كل نفس, one would expect «genitive».]
His saying لقد كنت فِي غَفلَة: it is an address to the disbelievers; it is also said: to the disbeliever and the believer; and it is also said: to the Prophet ﷺ.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying هَذَا مَا لدي عتيد: هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ما and عتيد are two khabars (predicates). It is also said: ما is the khabar, and عتيد is a badal (substitute) of ما, or a naʿt (adjective) of it, or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ. In ordinary speech, عتيدًا in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying ألقيا فِي جَهَنَّم: this is an address to the companion (القرين), and it was only put in the dual because He intended repetition, in the sense of "cast, cast" (ألقِ ألقِ). It is also said that it only came in the dual because the Arabs address the single person with the wording of the dual and with the wording of the plural. It is also said that it was put in the dual only because the fewest helpers of one who has standing and honour are two or more, so it was put in the dual on that basis. It is also said that it is only an address to the driver and the guardian (السائق والحافظ).
His saying الَّذِي جعل: الذي is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of كل, or by [an implied] أعني ("I mean"), or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar (predicate) being فألقياه.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying من خشِي الرَّحْمَن: من is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) of لكل, or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being ادخلوها; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "so it will be said to them: Enter it" (فيقال لهم ادخلوها).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying سرَاعًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the هاء and the ميم in عنهم, and the governing word in it is تشقق. It is also said that the meaning is "so they come out hastening" (فيخرجون سراعا), so it is a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in ويخرجون, and يخرجون is the governing word in it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ق﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
﴿والقرآن المجيد﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; القرآن: that by which the oath is sworn (muqsam bihi); المجيد: an adjective; the answer [to the oath] is omitted, indicated by what follows it, the implied form being: "you came to them as a warner of the resurrection, but they did not accept; rather, they wondered". And it has been said: it is mentioned, and they differed over what it is: it has been said that it is ﴿قد علمنا﴾, and it has been said that it is His words ﴿ما يلفظ من قول﴾, and it has been said: لتبعثن ("you will surely be resurrected") or لترجعن ("you will surely be returned"), according to what the context of the ayahs indicates.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿والنخل باسقات لها طلع نضيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; النخل is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات وحب الحصيد; باسقات: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of growing they were not tall; لها: a fronted khabar (predicate); طلع: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); نضيد: a naʿt (adjective) of طلع; the clause is a ḥāl from النخل الباسقات by way of succession (tarāduf), or from the pronoun in باسقات by way of overlapping (tadākhul).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿رزقا﴾: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it has the meaning of the maṣdar of أنبتنا, or: a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "given as provision to the servants", or "possessing provision".
﴿للعباد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ﴿رزقًا﴾.
﴿وأحيينا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فأنبتنا.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحيينا﴾.
﴿بلدة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ميتًا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).
﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf: a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar (predicate); ذلك: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address.
﴿الخروج﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative by the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وأصحاب الرس وثمود﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; كذبت: a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine; قبلهم: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبت; قوم نوح: fāʿil (agent); and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وعاد وفرعون وإخوان لوط﴾: also conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وأصحاب الأيكة وقوم تبع﴾: also conjoined (maʿṭūf); all of them have been dealt with before.
﴿كل كذب الرسل فحق وعيد﴾: كل: mubtadaʾ (subject); its tanwīn is in compensation for a word, i.e. "every messenger of those mentioned" [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests "every one (of the peoples) mentioned", since they are the ones who denied the messengers]; the clause كذب الرسل is its khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is a conjunction; حق: a past verb; وعيد: fāʿil (agent), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person; its original form is وعيدي, the yāʾ was dropped and the kasra remained as an indication of it.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, its implied form being: "Did We set about the creation and fail at it, so that anyone might imagine Us unable to repeat it?"; عيينا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بالخلق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عيينا; الأول: an adjective of الخلق; بل conjoins to something implied, the implied form being: "they do not deny Our power over the first creation; rather, they are in confusion and doubt about a new, fresh creation"; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); في لبس: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); من خلق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of لبس; جديد: a naʿt of خلق.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ولقد خلقنا الإنسان﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); خلقنا الإنسان: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl), with "نحن" ("We") implied; the clause ﴿نعلم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); or the wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive, with no grammatical position; ما: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿توسوس﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival), the implied form being: "and We know his soul's whispering to him"; ﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿توسوس﴾; نفسه: fāʿil.
﴿ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد﴾: نحن: the wāw is a conjunction; نحن: mubtadaʾ; أقرب: khabar; إليها [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah has ﴿إليه﴾]: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أقرب; من حبل الوريد: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to أقرب.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿إذ يتلقى المتلقيان عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقرب﴾ in the previous ayah, or a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, implied as اذكر ("remember"); the clause ﴿يتلقى﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿المتلقيان﴾: fāʿil (agent); ﴿عن اليمين﴾: a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿وعن الشمال﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿عن اليمين﴾; ﴿قعيد﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المتلقيان.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد﴾: ما: negative; يلفظ: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he", referring to man; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; قول: genitive in wording, accusative in position as the object of يلفظ; إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); لديه: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); رقيب: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); عتيد: a naʿt (adjective), nominative; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿يلفظ﴾; the clause ﴿ما يلفظ...﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; جاءت سكرة الموت: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بالحق: a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being clothed with the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa); and it has been said: it is for making transitive (taʿdiya); ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); ما: khabar (predicate); كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun; منه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تحيد﴾; the clause تحيد is the khabar of كان; the clause ﴿كنت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ذلك ما كنت is the object of an omitted saying.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿بل عجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم فقال الكافرون هذا شيء عجيب﴾: بل: a particle of conjunction and of digression (iḍrāb); عجبوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, i.e. "at the fact that there came to them"; منذر: the fāʿil of جاءهم; منهم: an adjective of منذر; فقال: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال الكافرون: a verb and its fāʿil; هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); شيء: khabar (predicate); عجيب: an adjective; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿ونفخ في الصور ذلك يوم الوعيد﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿وجاءت سكرة الموت﴾; نفخ: a passive past verb (built for an unnamed agent); في الصور: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نفخ﴾; ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); يوم الوعيد: its khabar (predicate); the demonstrative points to the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نفخ.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وجاءت كل نفس معها سائق وشهيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جاءت كل نفس: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); معها: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); سائق: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); شهيد is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to سائق; the nominal clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as an adjective of كل, or in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective of it, i.e. "with it is one who drives it and one who bears witness against it"; and you may make it a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "it will be said to every soul"; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun; في غفلة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كان; ﴿من هذا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿غفلة﴾; the fāʾ is a conjunction particle; كشفنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عنك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كشفنا﴾; غطاءك: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is a conjunction; بصرك: mubtadaʾ (subject); اليوم: an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); حديد: the khabar of بصرك.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; قال قرينه: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from ﴿هذا﴾; ﴿لدي﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. عتيد: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هذا﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار عنيد﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "it will be said: ألقيا"; ألقيا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn because it is attached to the alif of the dual; في جهنم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ألقيا; كل كفار: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عنيد: an adjective of كفار.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿مناع للخير معتد مريب﴾: مناع: a second naʿt (adjective) of كفار; للخير: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مناع﴾; معتد: another naʿt of كفار, genitive (majrūr) by an implied kasra on the yāʾ dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; مريب: another naʿt.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿الذي جعل مع الله إلها آخر﴾: ﴿الذي﴾ is a badal (substitute) from ﴿كل﴾ or from ﴿كفار﴾, or accusative (manṣūb) by way of censure (ʿalā al-dhamm), or a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause ﴿فألقياه﴾. The clause ﴿جعل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; ﴿مع الله﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إلهًا آخر﴾: the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فألقياه في العذاب الشديد﴾: the fāʾ is linking, because the relative noun resembles the conditional in generality; ألقياه: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of الذي if you make it a khabar; في العذاب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ألقياه﴾; الشديد: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿العذاب﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد﴾: قال قرينه: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ربنا: the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); ما: negative; أطغيته: a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لكن: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal) because it is lightened; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; في ضلال: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كان; بعيد: an adjective of ضلال; the clause ﴿قال قرينه﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿قال لا تختصموا لدي وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد﴾: قال: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; لا: prohibitive; تختصموا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لدي: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تختصموا﴾; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); قدمت: a verb and its fāʿil; إليكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدمت; the bāʾ in بالوعيد is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; or the verb falls on the clause of His words ﴿ما يبدل القول﴾, and بالوعيد is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "I sent this ahead to you clothed with the threat and joined to it", or "I sent it ahead to you, threatening you with it".

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿ما يبدل القول لدي وما أنا بظلام للعبيد﴾: ﴿ما﴾: negative; ﴿يبدل﴾: a passive imperfect verb (built for an unnamed agent); ﴿القول﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿لدي﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يبدل﴾; the wāw is a conjunction particle; ﴿ما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which operates like ليس; ﴿أنا﴾: the noun of ما; ﴿بظلام﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; ظلام: the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in wording; للعبيد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ظلام﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); إذا: an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; متنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause متنا is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it; what makes the adverb accusative is implied, its meaning being: "is it when we die and decay that we shall return?", because what follows indicates it; كنا: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, ﴿نا﴾ its noun, and ترابًا its khabar (predicate).
﴿ذلك رجع بعيد﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); رجع: khabar; بعيد: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظلام; نقول: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) "we"; لجهنم: a preposition and its genitive noun, genitive by the fatḥa because of being a proper noun and feminine, attached to نقول. هل: for interrogation; امتلأت: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; in امتلأتِ the tāʾ is the sign of the feminine, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring to جهنم].
﴿وتقول هل من مزيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; تقول: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil "she"; هل: for interrogation; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; مزيد: genitive in wording, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. هناك ("there"); the clause نقول is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; هل امتلأت is in the position of accusative as the object of نقول; تقول is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نقول; and هل من مزيد is in the position of accusative as the object of تقول.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وأزلفت الجنة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; أزلفت: a passive past verb (built for an unnamed agent); الجنة: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿للمتقين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أزلفت﴾.
﴿غير بعيد﴾: accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarfiyya), because it takes the place of the adverb, being its adjective, i.e. "a place not far"; and it has been said: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿هذا ما توعدون لكل أواب حفيظ﴾: هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); ما: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿توعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; لكل: a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) from His words ﴿للمتقين﴾ with repetition of the governing word; the clause ﴿هذا ما توعدون﴾ is parenthetical, separating the badal from that which it substitutes, with no grammatical position; or it is in the accusative by an implied saying, the implied saying being accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "it being said to them…".

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿من خشي الرحمن بالغيب﴾: ﴿من﴾: a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from ﴿كل﴾, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are the ones who feared", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ﴿ادخلوها بسلام﴾. The clause ﴿خشي الرحمن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. بالغيب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الرحمن﴾.
﴿وجاء بقلب منيب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جاء: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; بقلب: a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of ﴿جاء﴾; منيب: a naʿt (adjective), genitive; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined by the wāw to the ṣila clause.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿ادخلوها بسلام﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, as stated before; ادخلوها: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بسلام: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil, i.e. "safe from every fear", so it is a concurrent ḥāl (ḥāl muqārina).
﴿ذلك يوم الخلود﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); يوم الخلود: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿لهم ما يشاءون فيها﴾: لهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ما: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يشاءون is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, or attached to يشاءون.
﴿ولدينا مزيد﴾: لدينا: an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مزيد: a postponed mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أشد منهم بطشا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; كم: the declarative (khabariyya) kam, accusative (manṣūb) as an object by what follows it; أهلكنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); قبلهم: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من قرن: the tamyīz (specification) of the declarative kam; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); أشد: khabar (predicate); the clause is an adjective of كم or of its tamyīz; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أشد; بطشًا: a tamyīz; the clause ﴿وكم أهلكنا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فنقبوا في البلاد هل من محيص﴾: فنقبوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; نقبوا: a verb and its fāʿil; the conjoining is according to the meaning, as though: "their might grew strong, so they roamed"; في البلاد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نقبوا﴾; هل: an interrogative particle; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; محيص: genitive in wording, nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted, its implied form being "لهم" ("for them") or "لغيرهم" ("for others"); the clause هل من محيص is the object of an omitted saying, and the clause of saying is a ḥāl from the wāw of نقبوا, i.e. "so they roamed through the lands, saying: is there any escape?".

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); في ذلك: the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; ذكرى: the noun of إن; لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ذكرى; the clause كان is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. له: the fronted khabar of كان; قلب: its postponed noun; أو: a conjunction particle; ألقى السمع: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); شهيد: khabar.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿ولقد خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); خلقنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); السماوات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السماوات; في ستة أيام: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقنا; the clause ﴿ولقد خلقنا السماوات...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما مسنا من لغوب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما: negative; مسنا: a past verb, and نا is mafʿūl bihi; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; لغوب: genitive in wording, nominative in position because it is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿فاصبر على ما يقولون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); اصبر: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; على ما يقولون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿وسبح بحمد ربك﴾: سبح: an imperative verb; بحمد ربك: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of سبح, i.e. "pray, praising".
﴿قبل طلوع الشمس﴾: an adverb attached to سبح.
﴿وقبل الغروب﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the adverb.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); علمنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تنقص الأرض﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنقص; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); عندنا: an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); كتاب: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); حفيظ: an adjective; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من الليل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبح; the fāʾ is a conjunction; سبحه: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أدبار السجود: an adverb.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿واستمع يوم يناد المناد من مكان قريب﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; استمع: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you", and its object omitted, i.e. "and listen to the call of the caller"; the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استمع﴾. And it has been said: the implied object is "what I tell you", in which case يوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied ﴿يخرجون﴾ indicated by His words; المناد: fāʿil; من مكان: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينادي﴾; قريب: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق ذلك يوم الخروج﴾: the adverb is a badal (substitute) from the first adverb; the clause يسمعون is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of إذا to it [Translator's note: so in the source; the adverb here is ﴿يوم﴾, not إذا]; الصيحة: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالحق: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in يسمعون, or from الصيحة; ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); يوم الخروج: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; نحن: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause نحيي is the khabar (predicate) of إن, or the khabar of نحن, the [latter] clause then being the khabar of إن; إلينا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; المصير: a postponed mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم سراعا ذلك حشر علينا يسير﴾: the adverb is a badal (substitute) from what precedes it; some disallowed this because of its multiplicity, and attached it to المصير; the clause تشقق is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it; الأرض: fāʿil (agent); عنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تشقق﴾; سراعًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in عنهم; ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); حشر: khabar (predicate); علينا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يسير; and يسير is the khabar of ذلك.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿نحن أعلم بما يقولون﴾: ﴿نحن﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أعلم﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, i.e. "We know best that which they say"; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما يقولون﴾ is genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "their saying"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the clause ﴿يقولون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما أنت عليهم بجبار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; ﴿ما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which operates like ليس; ﴿أنت﴾: the noun of ما; ﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جبار﴾; ﴿بجبار﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿جبار﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in wording.
﴿فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); ذكر: an imperative verb; بالقرآن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ذكر﴾; من: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يخاف is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. وعيد: the object of يخاف; the yāʾ of the first person was dropped in conformity with the [Muṣḥaf] script.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فهم في أمر مريج﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and a conjunction of digression; كذبوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾; لما: temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya, "when"), or linking (rābiṭa); فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); أمر: khabar (predicate); مريج: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; ينظروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); إلى السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظروا﴾; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial); بنيناها: a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a badal (substitute) from السماء; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); ما: negative; لها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; فروج: genitive in wording, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) in position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; الأرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position of ﴿إلى السماء﴾, which is the accusative as an object; the clause مددناها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or ﴿الأرض﴾ is made accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "ومددنا الأرض" ("and We spread the earth"); ألقينا is conjoined to مددنا; فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ألقينا; رواسي: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. firmly-set, stable mountains.
﴿وأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج بهيج﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أنبتنا is also conjoined to what precedes; فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنبتنا; من كل زوج: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of an omitted object, the implied form being: "فأنبتنا فيها نباتًا كائنًا من كل زوج" ("and We caused to grow in it vegetation of every kind"); زوج: muḍāf ilayhi; بهيج: an adjective of زوج.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿تبصرة﴾: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of the preceding verbs in His words ﴿بنيناها وزيناها﴾ and His words ﴿مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها﴾, i.e. so that the actions mentioned and what they govern may be an insight; or: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "He gave them insight"; or: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. "giving insight"; or: a ḥāl from the object with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessing insight for whoever sees it".
﴿وذكرى﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿تبصرة﴾, accusative.
﴿لكل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تبصرة﴾.
﴿عبد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿منيب﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of عبد.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿ونزلنا من السماء ماء مباركا فأنبتنا به جنات وحب الحصيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; نزلنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزلنا; ماء: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مباركًا: an adjective; فأنبتنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نزلنا; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنبتنا; جنات: mafʿūl bihi; حب الحصيد is conjoined to جنات, and the qualified noun (mawṣūf) has been omitted.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
ق is not declined (muʿrab), because it is a letter of the alphabet. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned its meaning. وَالْقُرْآنِ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath. الْمَجِيدِ is its naʿt (adjective). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: «المجيد» means "the noble". As for the answer to the oath, there are four answers concerning it: al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: [it is] قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ [Qāf: 4]. Abū Isḥāq said: the answer is omitted, i.e. "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be resurrected (لتبعثنّ)". And it was said:
rather, what is omitted is what the context of the speech indicates, because they said: "This Prophet is a strange thing"; they were astonished that a man from the sons of Adam should be sent to them, so the threat fell upon that, i.e. "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely come to know the outcome of your denial on the Day of Resurrection", whereupon they said: أَإِذا مِتْنا. Abū Jaʿfar said: These are two answers. And whoever says:
"the meaning is: the matter has been decided, by Allah" — it does not need an answer, because the oath is placed in the middle, as you say: "I have spoken to you, by Allah, today." The fourth answer is that «ق» is a name for the mountain encompassing the earth; Wahb ibn Munabbih said that. The implied form would then be: "It is Qāf, by Allah", so on this view Qāf is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of the answers is that the answer is omitted because [the context] indicates it, since إذا متنا is an answer, and «إذا» must necessarily be attached (mutaʿalliq) to a verb, i.e. "Shall we be resurrected when…". As for the answer being قد علمنا, that is an error, because «قد» is not among the answers of oaths. And if Qāf is a name for the mountain, then the proper course with it is to decline it (iʿrāb).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ, i.e. they did not deny you because they did not know you to be truthful; rather, they were astonished that he came to them with the message of the Lord of the Worlds. فَقالَ الْكافِرُونَ هذا شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: أَإِذا مِتْنا, i.e. "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" وَكُنَّا تُراباً ذلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ: the meaning of بعيد according to al-Farrāʾ is "it will not happen". And that is well known in the language.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ, i.e. of their flesh and bodies. وَعِنْدَنا كِتابٌ حَفِيظٌ, in the sense of "preserving" (حافظ), because it does not wear away nor change.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ, i.e. they did not deny you because of anything that had become apparent to them. فَهُمْ فِي أَمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «مريج» means "objectionable"; and from him: "مريج: in error"; and from him: "مريج: discordant". Mujāhid and Qatāda said: "مريج: confused". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd said: "مريج: mixed up". Abū Jaʿfar said: These sayings, even though their wordings differ, are close in their meanings, because when a matter is discordant it is confused, objectionable and in error, since the truth is clear and evident.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: I.e. Have these polytheists, who denied the resurrection and rejected Our power to bring them back to life after decay, not looked at Our power to create the heaven, such that We made it a guarded roof? وَزَيَّنَّاها, i.e. with the stars. وَما لَها مِنْ فُرُوجٍ: [فروج] may be a plural, and may be a singular, i.e. "of any rifts and cracks".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْناها, i.e. "We spread it out". الأرض is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We spread out the earth". The nominative is permissible, except that the accusative is better, so that the verb is conjoined to a verb. وَأَلْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ, i.e. mountains that are anchored (رست) in the earth, i.e. are firm. وَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ, i.e. kind. Ibn ʿAbbās said:
بَهِيجٍ means "beautiful".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
تَبْصِرَةً is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "We did that in order to make you see the power of Allah, glory be to Him". وَذِكْرى, i.e. and so that you may remember the greatness of Allah and His authority, and so know that He is able to give life to the dead and to do whatever He wills.
لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ, i.e. one returning to faith and to obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَنَزَّلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً مُبارَكاً, which is the rain. فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ وَحَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ: al-Farrāʾ claimed that a thing has been annexed to itself, because in his view the grain (الحب) is the harvested (الحصيد). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate from the Basrans, among them Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, that annexing a thing to itself is impossible; rather, the implied form is "the grain of the harvested plant" (حبّ النبت الحصيد).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَالنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ, i.e. "and We caused the palm trees to grow tall". It is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl muqaddara): «باسقات» is [accusative] as a ḥāl. لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ: you make طلع nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), even though it is indefinite, because of the benefit [of information] in it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
رِزْقاً لِلْعِبادِ: Abū Isḥāq said: رزقا is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose).
وَأَحْيَيْنا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً, i.e. barren, with no crops or vegetation in it. كَذلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. your coming out of your graves is like this: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sends water and by it causes people to grow as crops grow. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "just as We created these things, We shall resurrect you".

nahhas-irab:12-14.t:
كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ, i.e. before these polytheists who denied Muḥammad ﷺ, the people of Nūḥ denied; the tāʾ is for the feminine of the collective. وَأَصْحابُ الرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوانُ لُوطٍ (13). وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ: Mujāhid said: الرّسّ is a well. Qatāda said: الأيكة is the dense, intertwined trees. وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ: all of it is conjunction (ʿaṭf). Abū Mijlaz said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās asked Kaʿb about Tubbaʿ, and he said: He was a righteous man; he took some young men from the rabbis and made them his intimates, and he became Muslim, and his people objected to that from him. And in the ḥadīth of Sahl ibn Saʿd from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «Do not curse Tubbaʿ, for he had become Muslim.» كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ: the implied form according to Sībawayh is "all of them" (كلّهم), then [the pronoun] was omitted because كلّ indicates it. All the grammarians permitted "كلّ منطلق" in the sense of "all of them are departing". Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd permit dropping the nunation (tanwīn), saying "كلّ منطلق" in the sense of "all of them", treating it as a ghāya (a word cut off from its annexed term) like قبل and بعد. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: This is the speech of someone who does not know why قبل and بعد are made indeclinable (mabnī), and [what is] analogous to this among the words, because the grammarians have restricted [this] to the adverbs (ẓurūf) on account of the cause that is in them and not in other [words]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear and correct statement according to the people of Arabic.
The yāʾ was dropped from وَعِيدِ because it is the end of a verse, so that the verses do not differ. As for the one who retains it in continuous reading (al-idrāj) and drops it in pause, his argument is that the pause is a place of dropping; the proof of that is that you say لم يمض, and when you continue [the speech] you give the ḍād a kasra and nothing else. The meaning of فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ is: so the threat from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, of punishment in the Hereafter and of retribution became binding upon the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ: one says "عيينا بالأمر" and "عييّ به" when one could not find one's way in it and did not master it. When you say عيينا, assimilation (idghām) is not permitted, because the second letter is vowelless, so if you assimilated it into the first two vowelless letters would meet. As for the meaning, it was said to those who denied the resurrection and said (ذلك رجع بعيد): "Were We wearied by the initial creation, so that We should be wearied by bringing you back to life after decay?" ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās:
أفعيينا بالخلق الأول — he said: He is saying, "We were not wearied by it." Abū Jaʿfar said: And thus the interrogative that contains the meaning of affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke takes on the meaning of negation, i.e. He was not wearied by the first creation. بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ, i.e. about the resurrection.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ: the pronoun in به refers back to «ما». Al-Farrāʾ permitted that it refer to الإنسان, i.e. "and He knows what his soul whispers to him". وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ: Ibn ʿAbbās said: الوريد is the vein of the neck. The grammarians have two implied readings of it: al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: "And We are nearer to him in power than the jugular vein". Someone else said: i.e. "And We are nearer to him in knowledge of what his soul whispers to him than the jugular vein".

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: And He did not say قعيدان (two seated ones); there are several answers to this. The school of Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī is that the meaning is "on the right a seated one and on the left a seated one", and then [one of them] was omitted. The school of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ is that «قعيد» is a singular that stands for two and for more than two, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا [Ghāfir: 67]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the implied form in قَعِيدٌ is that it is intended to be placed earlier, i.e. "on the right a seated one", and then "and on the left" is conjoined to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is clear and good, and similar to it is وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ [al-Tawba: 62]. A fourth view is that قعيد is in the sense of a group, as the Arabs use the faʿīl pattern; He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ [al-Taḥrīm: 4].

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ما يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ: the pronoun in it refers back to الإنسان, i.e. man does not utter any word, speaking it, except that at [the moment] he utters it there is رَقِيبٌ, i.e. a guardian who records it against him. عَتِيدٌ means "prepared" (معدّ). This is among the uses of the faʿīl pattern: it can have the sense of a plural, the sense of mufʿal, the sense of mafʿūl, like قتيل (killed), and the sense of fāʿil, like قدير in the sense of قادر (able).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ, i.e. its intensity and its overpowering of a person's understanding, so that he becomes like one drunk from drink or from sleep. بِالْحَقِّ, i.e. with the matter of the Hereafter, which is true, until he sees it clearly with his own eyes. Another view is that الحقّ is death, i.e. "and the stupor of death came with the reality of death". It is soundly reported from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read «وجاءت سكرة الحقّ بالموت», and likewise from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Allah's mercy be upon him. He said: This is a reading by way of explanation (tafsīr). There are two views on its meaning: الحقّ may be Allah, Majestic and Mighty, i.e. "and the stupor [from] Allah came with death"; the other view is that of al-Farrāʾ: the stupor is itself the truth, "and the stupor, the truth, came", a thing annexed to itself. ذلِكَ ما كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ, i.e. that stupor is what you used to flee from. As for the masculine [ذلك], it is in the sense of "that drunkenness" (ذلك السّكر).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: I.e. what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, threatened the disbelievers and the people of sins with: the Fire.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: It is construed according to the meaning; had it been according to the wording, it would have been «وجاء كلّ نفس معه». The implied form is «ومعها»; the wāw was omitted because of the returning pronoun, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا: the people of knowledge differed as to whom this address is directed, and they have three views on it. Zayd ibn Aslam and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said that this address is to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related from Yaʿqūb from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: I said to Zayd ibn Aslam, "And is this address to the Prophet ﷺ?" He said: "What do you find objectionable in this, when Allah, glory be to Him, has said: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوى وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدى [al-Ḍuḥā: 6, 7]?" He said: So this is one view. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا — he said: This is an address to the disbelievers. Mujāhid said the same. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: an address to the polytheists. Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, after objecting to what Zayd ibn Aslam said, said: "He is not knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs, nor does he have [that]; rather, this is an address to the disbelievers."
These are two views. The third view is what al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said:
This is an address to the righteous and the wicked; and it is the view of Qatāda. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the view of Zayd ibn Aslam, its interpretation is that in his view the speech is complete at His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَجاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَها سائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ (21); then He began anew: "O Muḥammad, you were heedless of this religion and of what was revealed to you, before you were sent, when you were in the Jāhiliyya". فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ, i.e. "so We made you see". فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ, i.e. "so your knowledge is penetrating".
Sight (البصر) here is in the sense of knowledge. The most fitting thing said about the verse is that it is general, for the righteous and the wicked; what indicates that is وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ, for this is general for all people, righteous and wicked. Thus it is known that the meaning of وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ is "and the stupor of death came to you, O man"; then the address continues on this [basis] in لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا, i.e. "you were, O man, heedless of what you have now seen with your eyes". If he was a doer of good, he regrets that he did not do more; and if he was an evildoer, he regrets that he did not desist. This is when the covering has been removed from both of them, so "your sight today is penetrating" for what you have seen. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "فبصرك: the tongue of the balance."
It was said: some scholars interpreted this as a likeness for justice, i.e. "you are the one of Allah's creatures, Majestic and Mighty, who knows best your own deeds, so your sight of them is like the tongue of the balance by which excess and deficiency are known".

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: «قرينه» is his driver who has been put in charge of him. هذا ما لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ: he said: this is what he took and brought. هذا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and عَتِيدٌ is a second khabar. It may be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ; it may be a badal (substitute) from «ما»; and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of ما, if you make «ما» indefinite. The accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an, like وَهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً [Hūd: 72].

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
The grammarians differed concerning His saying ألقيا. Some said: it is an address to the companion (القرين), i.e. it is said to the companion: ألقيا. This is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, and he claimed that the Arabs address one person with the address for two, saying "O man, stand (قوما)!", and he recited [in the ṭawīl metre]:
432-
خليليّ مرّا بي على أمّ جندب ... لنقضي حاجات الفؤاد المعذّب
(My two friends, pass with me by Umm Jundab, that we may fulfil the needs of the tormented heart.)
 He was addressing only one person, and he inferred that from his saying [in the ṭawīl metre]: 433-
ألم تر أنّي كلما جئت طارقا ... وجدت بها طيبا وإن لم تطيّب
(Have you not seen that whenever I came by night, I found fragrance in her, even though she was not perfumed?)
Others said: «قرين» is used for a group, for one and for two, like وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd from Bakr ibn Muḥammad al-Māzinī, who said: The Arabs say to one person قوما on one condition: when they mean repetition of the verb, i.e. "stand, stand" (قم قم); so they brought the alif to indicate this meaning, and likewise «ألقيا». Another view: it is an address to two. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: [it is addressed to] the driver and the guardian together. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said:
العنيد is the one who shuns the truth and who stubbornly opposes Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: عنيد is in the sense of معاند (stubborn opponent), like ضجيع (bedfellow) and جليس (sitting companion).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ, i.e. of what is obligatory upon him, of zakāt and other things; and الخير is wealth. ومُعْتَدٍ: [aggressing] against people with his tongue and his hand. Qatāda said: مُرِيبٍ means "doubting".

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ: «الذي» may be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from كلّ, or in the sense of "I mean" (أعني); and it may be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is فَأَلْقِياهُ فِي الْعَذابِ الشَّدِيدِ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: قالَ قَرِينُهُ رَبَّنا ما أَطْغَيْتُهُ, i.e. "I did not make him a transgressor (طاغيا)", i.e. one who oversteps into disbelief. وَلكِنْ كانَ فِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ, i.e. on a path deviating from the truth.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: قالَ لا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: They offered excuses without any [valid] excuse, so He invalidated their argument against them. وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِالْوَعِيدِ, i.e. with the threat in which there is no injustice and which will not be broken; so do not dispute before Me.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ما يُبَدَّلُ الْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ: Mujāhid said: i.e. "I have decreed what I decree". وَما أَنَا بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ, i.e. "I do not seize anyone for another's crime".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ: the governing word (ʿāmil) in يوم is ظلام. وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ: there are two views on its meaning. One of them is that the meaning is "there is no more" (ما في مزيد), and the holder of this view argues from His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ [al-Sajda: 13; Ṣād: 85]. This is the view of ʿIkrima, and analogous to it is the ḥadīth when it was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Will you not stay in one of your houses?" and he said: «And has ʿAqīl left us any house?», i.e. he did not leave us a house, for he sold it at the time of the Hijra. So this is one view. The other view is فهل من مزيد as a request for more. This is the view of Anas ibn Mālik, and what indicates it is the sound ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: «Jahannam will keep saying "Is there any more?", and the Lord of the Worlds, glory be to Him and exalted, will place His foot in it, and it will say: "Enough, enough (قط قط)."» Abū Jaʿfar said: This ḥadīth has a sound chain of transmission (isnād), and it indicates the opposite of the first view. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: I.e. near for the God-fearing, i.e. those who guard themselves against disobeying Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ, i.e. this which We have described for the God-fearing is what you are promised. لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ: Ibn Zayd said: for every one who repents, returning to Allah in obedience to Him. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: أَوَّابٍ means one who glorifies [Allah]; and from him: حَفِيظٍ, one who remembered his sins until he repented of them. Qatāda said: «حفيظ» means one who preserves what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, entrusted him with; and the meaning of this is that he guarded his limbs from disobeying Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «كلّ», and it may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with خَشِيَ in the position of the jussive as the condition (sharṭ). The implied form is: خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ, so it will be said to them: ادْخُلُوها — according to the meaning of من, while what precedes it is according to its wording. مُنِيبٍ: one who repents, returning to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ, i.e. that which We have described for the God-fearing is a day from which they will never depart.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: لَهُمْ ما يَشاؤُنَ فِيها, i.e. they will have whatever they want, and more by way of honour. Anas ibn Mālik explained the meaning of وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ — and since [such a thing] cannot be taken by personal suggestion and can only be taken from the Prophet, upon him be peace — concerning وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ he said: He said: «The Lord of the Worlds will manifest Himself to them and say: By My might, I shall manifest Myself to you so that you look at Me. And He will say: Welcome to My servants, My neighbours, My visitors and My delegation; look at Me.» That is the utmost of giving and the bounty of the "more".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ, i.e. before the polytheists of Quraysh who denied you. هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً: those destroyed were stronger than those who denied you. [بطشا] is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz). فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ means "they left their traces", and its literal meaning in the language is "they roamed about and penetrated deep".
هَلْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "Did they have any escape from death?", and كان was omitted because [the context] indicates it. The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar فَنَقَّبُوا is anomalous (shādhdh), departing from the majority, and it is by way of threat. [Translator's note: the variant is printed here with the same spelling as the standard reading; the source does not show how Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar's variant differs in vowelling; the remark "by way of threat" suggests an imperative.]

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى, i.e. in Our destruction of the generations whom We destroyed and whose story We have related.
لَذِكْرى: by which one who has a heart with which he understands is reminded. أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ, i.e. listened attentively. وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ: understanding, not heedless; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
The hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) was kept in ستة because it is a number for a masculine [noun], and you distinguish between it and the feminine. The meaning of يوم is:
a period of time; that is why it is mentioned before the creation of daytime. وَما مَسَّنا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ: from لغب يلغب and يلغب, when one becomes tired.

nahhas-irab:39-40.t:
فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ — for I am lying in wait for them — وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ. The people of tafsīr said: He means by it the Jews, because they said "He rested on the Sabbath day". He, Majestic and Mighty, said: "So be patient over what they say, for I am lying in wait for them", وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ — the people of tafsīr took it in the sense of prayer, and likewise وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ. Ibn Zayd said: [it is] the ʿatama (night prayer). Mujāhid said: the whole night. It was said: He means the Maghrib and the later ʿIshāʾ. He said:
This is more fitting, because of the generality of "the night" in the apparent sense of the verse. وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ: there are two views on it. Ibn Zayd said:
the supererogatory prayers (nawāfil). He said: This is a clear view, because the verse is general, so it is taken as general unless some proof comes [to restrict it]; except that the argument of the majority has come [to the effect] that the meaning of وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ is two rakʿas after Maghrib. That was said by ʿUmar, ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them, and among the Successors by al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Some of the ḥadīth scholars trace the ḥadīth of ʿAlī back to the Prophet ﷺ: (وإدبار السجود) — he said: «two rakʿas after Maghrib». Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ with a fatḥa on the hamza, making it the plural of دبر; and whoever says إدبار makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of أدبر. They all agreed on the kasra in وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ [al-Ṭūr: 49]. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that prostration has no "going back" (إدبار). This is among the things held against him, because the meaning of وأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ is "what comes after it and what follows it", so this applies to prostration, and the stars and man are the same [in this respect]. The eminent ḥadīth scholars have related the explanation of وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ and وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ, and we do not know of any of them who distinguished between the two.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ without a yāʾ, both in continuous reading and in pause; and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, following the script. Some opposed him and said: there is no change of the script in this, because the yāʾ is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) of the verb, so it is known that its due is to remain. Sībawayh said: what is good in the like of this is retaining the yāʾ in pause and in continuous reading. He said: and it is permissible to drop it in pause. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is because you say مناد, then you add the alif and lām, and you do not change the noun from its state. As for the meaning of وَاسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ (41),
it was said concerning it: i.e. "[listen for] the time of the day". Kaʿb said: The caller is an angel who calls from a near place, from the Rock of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), with a loud voice: "O decayed bones and severed joints, gather together for the final judgement!"

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ, i.e. with the gathering for the reckoning. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ: from their graves.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ: the object is omitted, i.e. "We give life to the dead and cause the living to die". وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ, i.e. the return.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِراعاً: the governing word (ʿāmil) in «يوم» is المصير, i.e. "and to Us is their return on the day [the earth] splits apart (تتشقّق)".
