In تَشَقَّقُ the tāʾ was assimilated into the shīn; and whoever says تشقّق dropped the tāʾ. سِراعاً is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it was said: from the hāʾ and the mīm [of عنهم]; and it was said: a ḥāl from the hāʾ and the mīm is not permissible, because there is no governing word over it; rather, the implied form is "so they come out hastening" (فيخرجون سراعا). ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنا يَسِيرٌ, i.e. easy.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ (45). نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ, i.e. of the fabrication and the denial of the resurrection. وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ, i.e. "one given authority [over them]". Al-Farrāʾ said: جبّار has been put in the place of سلطان (one with authority). Whoever says that بجبّار means "you do not compel them (تجبرهم) to what you want" is mistaken, because the faʿʿāl pattern is not formed from afʿala; and even though al-Farrāʾ related that one says درّاك from أدرك, this is anomalous and unknown. He also related "جبرت الرجل" (I compelled the man), and this is among the anomalies, even though some of the jurists are fond of جبرت. فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ, i.e. My threat to whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command.

safi-cedvel:28-30.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is a prohibitive particle that puts the verb in the jussive (majzūm). (لديّ) is an indeclinable (mabnī) adverb in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تختصموا). (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (إليكم) is attached to (قدّمت). (بالوعيد) is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent (fāʿil) of قدّمت or from its implied object [Note: Some of them hold that (الباء) is redundant (zāʾida) in the object.].
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive (istināfiyya).
And the clause: «لا تختصموا ... » is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what was said (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «قدّمت ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: The meaning: Do not dispute, for it is now established with you that I put the warning before you.].
29- (ما) is negative. (لديّ) is like the first one, attached to (يبدّل). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative, working like ليس. (ظلّام) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما. (اللام) is redundant, for reinforcement. (العبيد) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of ظلّام.
And the clause: «ما يبدّل القول ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «ما أنا بظلّام ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «ما يبدل ...».
30- (يوم) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ظلّام). (لجهنّم) is attached to (نقول). (هل) is an interrogative particle in both places. (مزيد) is genitive in form by مِن and nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is there any more there?" [Note: The question is either for affirmation and information, i.e. "I have had enough", or for a request, i.e. "give me more".].
And the clause: «نقول ... » is in the position of the genitive, being a muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause: «هل امتلأت ... » is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «تقول ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نقول.
And the clause: «هل من مزيد» is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what was said.

* Morphology:
(مزيد) is a maṣdar mīmī (verbal noun with initial mīm) from the triliteral verb زاد, on the pattern مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, which is irregular (against the norm); then ʿilāl (weak-letter change) affected it by making the vowel quiescent, so the vowel of its ʿayn was moved to its fāʾ and the ʿayn became quiescent. It may also be a noun of place from the triliteral زاد.

* Rhetoric:
Tamthīl (representation): in His words, Exalted is He, «يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ».
A question and an answer, brought in the manner of representation and imaginative depiction, to magnify the dread of it. The meaning is that, despite its vastness and the great distance between its sides, people and jinn are thrown into it, troop after troop, until it is full; or that it is so vast that those who enter it enter it and there remains in it still an empty place; or that, in its rage against the disobedient, it asks for more of them.
This is among the beauty and marvels of sensory imagination and of giving Hell a body: enraged and ravenous, never sated, with those who in their worldly life stopped their ears to the call to guidance, and persisted in their error and obstinacy, rushing headlong into it.

* Benefits:
- The clause that falls in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa)..
The Almighty's words occur in this verse: يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ. The clause (نقول) is in the position of the genitive by annexation, because it occurs after the adverb. We shall set out below what relates to this clause. Only eight things are annexed to a clause:
1- Nouns of time: as in His words, Exalted is He: وَالسَّلامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ and His words, Exalted is He: لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ يَوْمَ هُمْ بارِزُونَ. Among nouns of time there are three whose annexation to a clause is obligatory:
(إذ) by agreement, (إذا) according to the majority, and (لما) according to those who say it is a noun.
2- حيث: it is distinguished in this from all other nouns of place; its annexation to a clause is obligatory, and it is not a condition that it be an adverb, as in His words, Exalted is He: وَامْضُوا حَيْثُ تُؤْمَرُونَ.
3- آية in the sense of "sign": it is annexed, permissibly, to a verbal clause whose verb is fully conjugable, affirmed or negated by ما, as in the poet's verse:
بآية يقدمون الخيل شعثا ... كأنّ على سنابكها مداما
(By a sign they lead the horses, dishevelled, as though on their hooves there were wine.)
and his verse:
ألكني إلى قومي السلام رسالة ... بآية ما كانوا ضعافا ولا عزلا
(Carry for me to my people the greeting as a message, by the sign that they were neither weak nor unarmed.)
ألكني: "convey". The verse is by ʿAmr ibn Shaʾs.
4- (ذو) in their saying: «اذهب بذي تسلم»; the باء here is locative (ẓarfiyya), and ذي is an adjective of an omitted word for "time". Then most say it means "possessor", so the described noun is indefinite, i.e. "go at a time possessing safety" (that is, at a time that is likely to bring safety).
5- لدن and 6- ريث: these two are annexed, permissibly, to a verbal clause whose verb is fully conjugable, and it is required that it be affirmed, unlike the case with آية.
As for لدن, it is a noun for the starting point of a limit, whether of time or of place. Among its attestations is the poet's verse:
لزمنا لدن سألتمونا وفاقكم ... فلا يك منكم للخلاف جنوح
(We have kept to agreement with you since you asked us for it, so let there be no inclination to discord on your side.)
As for ريث, it is the maṣdar of راث, "to be slow", and it was treated like the nouns of time in being annexed to a clause, just as maṣdars were treated like nouns of time in giving a time-limit, as in your saying «جئتك صلاة العصر» ("I came to you at the afternoon prayer"). The poet said:
خليلىّ رفقا ريث أقضى لبانة ... من العرصات المذكرات عهودا
(My two friends, gently, while I fulfil a need at the courtyards that recall past times.)
7 and 8: (قول) and (قائل): as in the poet's verse:
قول يا للرجال ينهض منا ... مسرعين الكهول والشبانا
(At the cry "O men!" the middle-aged and the young among us rise, hastening.)
and the poet's verse:
وأجبت قائل كيف أنت بصالح ... حتى مللت وملّني عوّادي
(I answered the one who said "How are you?" with "Well", until I grew weary and my visitors grew weary of me.)

safi-cedvel:31-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (للمتّقين) is attached to (أزلفت). (غير) is an adverb of place standing in for the implied adverb, i.e. "a place not far", so it is its adjective [Note: or it is a ḥāl from الجنّة, reinforcing its governing element ... and بعيد was not made feminine either because it is of the pattern فعيل in which masculine and feminine are alike, or by taking الجنّة to include the sense of "garden", or by intending the place of Paradise..].
Clause: «أزلفت الجنّة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
32-34- (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هذا), the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted; (الواو) in (توعدون) is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil). (لكلّ) is a badal (substitute) for المتقين, with the preposition repeated. (من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, a badal for (كلّ) [Note: or it is a mubtadaʾ in the position of the nominative whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: "It will be said to them: enter it in peace."]. (بالغيب) is a ḥāl from الرحمن, i.e. "while unseen". (بقلب) is a ḥāl from the agent of جاء. (بسلام) is a ḥāl from the agent of ادخلوها.. (يوم) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك), and the demonstrative refers to the time of entering.
And the clause: «هذا ما توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya).
And the clause: «توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «خشي الرحمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause: «جاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خشي.
And the clause: «ادخلوها ... » is in the position of the accusative, being the content of an implied, resumptive saying.
And the clause: «ذلك يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
(لهم) is attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (ما), the returning pronoun being omitted. (فيها) is attached to (يشاءون) [Note: or to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun.]. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لدينا) is an indeclinable adverb in the position of the accusative, attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مزيد).
And the clause: «لهم ما يشاءون ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of ادخلوها, and it contains an iltifāt (shift of person), i.e. "you shall have therein what you wish" [Note: It may be resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
And the clause: «يشاءون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «لدينا مزيد» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لهم ما يشاءون.

* Morphology:
(34) الخلود: a samāʿī (heard, not rule-derived) maṣdar of the verb خلد, of the bāb of نصر, meaning "to endure"; its pattern is فعول with two ḍammas.

* Rhetoric:
Eloquent praise: in His words, Exalted is He, «مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ».
Here He coupled fear with His name that indicates the breadth of mercy, as eloquent praise of the one who fears: he fears Him although he knows that He is vast in mercy, and he is praised as one who fears although the One feared is unseen. Similar is «وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ ما آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ», where He describes them as fearful despite their abundant acts of obedience. The heart is described as turning back (ināba), which is returning to Allah the Exalted, because what counts is what is established of it in the heart.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (كم) is khabariyya (declarative, not interrogative), an indeclinable word in the position of the accusative, a fronted direct object. (من قبلهم) is attached to (أهلكنا). (من قرن) is the tamyīz (specification) of كم. (منهم) is attached to (أشدّ). (بطشا) is an accusative tamyīz. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (في البلاد) is attached to (نقّبوا). (هل) is an interrogative particle. (محيص) is genitive in form by the redundant مِن and nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "for them".
Clause: «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «هم أشدّ ... » is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of قرن.
And the clause: «نقّبوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause هم أشدّ ...
And the clause: «هل من محيص ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: It may be the content of an implied saying that is a ḥāl from the agent of نقّبوا ... i.e. "they searched about, saying: Is there any escape?"].

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(في ذلك) is attached to an omitted element, the khabar of إنّ. (اللام) is the lām of emphasis. (ذكرى) is the ism (noun) of إنّ, accusative. (لمن) is attached to (ذكرى). (له) is attached to the khabar of كان. (أو) is a conjunction. (الواو) is circumstantial.
Clause: «إنّ في ذلك لذكرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «كان له قلب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause: «ألقى السمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «هو شهيد» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:38-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لقد خلقنا ... ) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (16) of this sūra.]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, conjoined to السموات. (بينهما) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of ما. (في ستّة) is attached to (خلقنا). (الواو) is circumstantial. (ما) is negative. (لغوب) is genitive in form by a redundant مِن and nominative in position, the agent of مسّنا.
Clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ما مسّنا من لغوب» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
39- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive attached to (اصبر), the returning pronoun being omitted.]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places..
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون..) is in the position of the genitive after (على), attached to (اصبر).
(بحمد) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سبّح. (قبل) is an accusative adverb attached to (سبّح) in both places.
And the clause: «اصبر ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you hear the denial of the disbelievers, then be patient".
And the clause: «سبّح ... » is conjoined to the clause اصبر.
40- (الواو) is a conjunction. (من الليل) is attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is سبّحه or قم. (الفاء) is redundant, or a conjunction. (أدبار) is conjoined to the adverb قبل [Note: or conjoined to the position of (من الليل), which is the accusative.].
And the clause: «(قم أو سبّحه) من الليل» is conjoined to the clause اصبر.
And the clause: «سبّحه ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative (tafsīriyya), or it is conjoined to the clause قم. 41- (الواو) is a conjunction, and the object of (استمع) is omitted, its implied form being "my word" or "what I say". (يوم) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is يخرجون [Note: or يعلمون, the outcome of their denial.], indicated by His words ذلك يوم الخروج. (يناد) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, in keeping with the reading in continuous speech (waṣl). (المناد) is the agent, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, following the written form (rasm) or because of the pause. (من مكان) is attached to (ينادي)..
And the clause: «استمع ... » is conjoined to the clause اصبر.
And the clause: «(يخرجون..)» (implied) has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ينادي المنادي» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
42- (يوم) is a badal of the first, accusative like it. (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يسمعون [Note: or to a ḥāl from الصيحة ... and al-Maḥallī explained (الحقّ) as the resurrection, and on this the preposition and its noun are attached to (يسمعون) and the باء is for transitivity.]. (ذلك يوم الخروج) the i'rab of its like has already been given [Note: in verse (34) of this sūra.].
And the clause: «يسمعون ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ذلك يوم الخروج» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istinaf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(38) ستة: the noun of the known number. It came in the feminine because its counted noun is masculine; its pattern is فعلة with kasra and then sukūn.
(40) السجود: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb سجد; its pattern is فعول with two ḍammas.
(يناد) the word was written with the yāʾ dropped, in keeping with the reading in continuous speech; (المناد) its final yāʾ was dropped, following the written form or the pause.

safi-cedvel:43-44.t:
* I'rab:
(نحن) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ [Note: or a pronoun "استعمر" [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for استعير, "borrowed"] for the position of the accusative, as emphasis (tawkīd) of the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ.]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (إلينا) is attached to a fronted khabar.
Clause: «إنّا نحن نحيي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «نحن نحيي ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «نميت» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause نحيي.
And the clause: «إلينا المصير» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause نميت.
44- (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (المصير) [Note: or attached to الخروج in verse (42), and on this the clause انّا نحن نحيي.. is parenthetical.]. (تشقّق) is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs was dropped. (عنهم) is attached to (تشقّق). (سراعا) is an accusative ḥāl, its governing element implied, i.e. "they come out hastening". The demonstrative in (ذلك) points to the meaning of the gathering that is announced, namely bringing back to life after death and the assembling for the presentation.. (علينا) is attached to the adjective (يسير) [Note: Separating the adjective from the described noun by a preposition and its noun, for the sense of restriction, is permissible.].
And the clause: «تشقّق الأرض ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ذلك حشر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(سراعا) is the plural of سريع, a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from (سرع) of the bāb of كرم or of فرح; its pattern is فعيل, and the pattern of سراع is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(حشر) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb حشر; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa and then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted]. (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative, working like ليس. (عليهم) is attached to (جبّار), which is genitive in form by the (الباء) and accusative in position, the khabar of ما. (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause. (بالقرآن) is attached to (ذكّر). (وعيد) is the direct object of the verb of fear, accusative, the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, to suit the verse-ending (fāṣila)..
Clause: «نحن أعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون..) is in the position of the genitive by the باء, attached to (أعلم), which is not here a comparative.
And the clause: «ما أنت عليهم بجبّار» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «ذكّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "be alert, and remind".
And the clause: «يخاف» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is the wāw of oath. (القرآن) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear).
The clause « (أقسم) بالقرآن ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).. The answer to the oath is omitted, implied according to the context of the speech, i.e. "لقد أرسلنا محمّدا" (We have indeed sent Muḥammad), or "ما آمن كفّار مكّة بمحمّد ﷺ" (the disbelievers of Mecca did not believe in Muḥammad ﷺ).

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, Exalted is He, «وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ».
He described it thus because it is the speech of the Majestic One, so it is a description with the attribute of its speaker. The attribution is therefore figurative, as in القرآن الحكيم; or because whoever knows its meanings and acts by what is in it becomes glorious with Allah, Exalted is He, and with people.

safi-cedvel:2-3.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for abandonment (iḍrāb). (أن) is a maṣdar particle. (منهم) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (منذر)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءهم..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (عجبوا).
(الفاء) is a conjunction. (الهمزة) is for interrogation of astonishment. (إذا) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the position of accusative attached to the omitted apodosis, i.e. "we shall return".
The clause «عجبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «جاءهم منذر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «قال الكافرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هذا شيء ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.
The clause «متنا ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كنّا ترابا ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause متنا.. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "نرجع" (shall we return) or "فهل نرجع؟" (so shall we return?).
The clause «ذلك رجع بعيد ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption within the scope of the disbelievers' saying.

* Morphology:
(رجع) is a samāʿī (heard, non-systematic) maṣdar of the triliteral verb رجع of the bāb ضرب. Its pattern is فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) is a particle of confirmation. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the direct object, with the returning pronoun omitted. (منهم) is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun [Note: or attached to (تنقص).]. (الواو) is a conjunction, or circumstantial. (عندنا) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كتاب).
The clause «علمنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تنقص الأرض ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «عندنا كتاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.].
5- (بل) is for transitional abandonment. (بالحقّ) is attached to (كذّبوا). (لمّا) is an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the content of the apodosis. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (في أمر) is attached to an omitted element that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «جاءهم ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "when the truth came to them, they denied it".
The clause «هم في أمر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوا..

* Morphology:
(مريج) is a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral مرج in the sense of "was disturbed". In al-Mukhtār: "مرج الأمر والدين" means it became confused, of the bāb طرب; and "أمر مريج" is a confused matter. Its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation of rebuke. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (إلى السماء) is attached to (ينظروا). (فوقهم) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to a ḥāl from السماء. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (بنيناها). (ما) is negative. (لها) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (فروج) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «ينظروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Were they heedless, so they did not look ...".
The clause «بنيناها ... » is in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) from السماء.
The clause «زيّناها ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause بنيناها.
The clause «ما لها من فروج» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause بنيناها [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the object in (زيّناها).].
7- 8- (الواو) is resumptive. (الأرض) is the direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "مددنا" (We spread) [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed it to be conjoined to the position of (السماء), i.e. "Have they not seen the heaven and the earth".]. (فيها) is attached to (ألقينا), and the second is attached to (أنبتنا). (من كلّ) is an adjective (naʿt) of the omitted direct object of أنبتنا, i.e. "We caused to grow vegetation of every pair", or "kinds of every pair". (تبصرة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb [Note: or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl from the object of أنبتنا, or a ḥāl with an implied muḍāf, i.e. "possessing insight" ...
or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with أنبتنا as governor.]. (لكلّ) is attached to (ذكرى)..
The clause « (مددنا) الأرض ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «مددناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الأرض if it is conjoined to the position of السماء.].
The clause «ألقينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (مددنا).
The clause «أنبتنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (مددنا).
9- (الواو) is a conjunction. (من السماء) is attached to (نزّلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (به) is attached to (أنبتنا), and (الباء) is causal..
The clause «نزّلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause "مددنا الأرض" [Note: or resumptive, if there is no clause to be joined to according to the other analysis.].
The clause «أنبتنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نزّلنا.
10- (الواو) is a conjunction. (النخل) is conjoined to جنّات, or to حبّ. (باسقات) is a ḥāl from النخل [Note: it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), since they were not tall at the time of growing.], accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra. (لها) is attached to a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (طلع)..
The clause «لها طلع ... » is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl from النخل.
11- (رزقا) is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "provided" [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, because it meets it in meaning, since causing to grow is provision ... or a ḥāl with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing provision" .... Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.]. (للعباد) is attached to (رزقا) [Note: or attached to an adjective of (رزقا).]. (به) is attached to (أحيينا), and (الباء) is causal. (ميتا) is an adjective (naʿt) of بلدة, accusative; it came masculine with regard to the sense of "place". (كذلك) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الخروج).
The clause «أحيينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أنبتنا.
The clause «كذلك الخروج» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(6) فروج: the plural of فرج in the sense of "cleft". Its pattern is فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn), and the plural is فعول (with two ḍammas).
(9) الحصيد: a noun in the sense of the harvested part of the crop. Its pattern is فعيل.
(10) باسقات: the plural of باسقة, feminine of باسق, an active participle from the triliteral بسق. Its pattern is فاعل..
(نضيد) is a derived adjective from the triliteral نضد of the bāb ضرب, meaning that part of it was joined to another. Its pattern is فعيل in the sense of مفعول, or it is an intensive of the active participle.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the modified noun (al-mawṣūf)..
It occurs in the styles of the Arabs that the modified noun is omitted and the adjective kept as an indication of it, as in the verse we are dealing with, in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ وَحَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ». الحصيد is an adjective of the plant and has stood in for it, the implied form being: "وحب النبت الحصيد". Of this is His saying, Exalted is He: «وَعِنْدَهُمْ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ», i.e. "حور قاصرات". «وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ أَنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ», i.e. "دروعا سابغات". «فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً», i.e. "ضحكا قليلا وبكاء كثيرا". «وَلَدارُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ», i.e. "ولدار الحياة الآخرة".
Suḥaym ibn Wathīl said:
(أنا ابن جلا وطلاع الثنايا ... متى أضع العمامة تعرفوني) (I am the son of one who has unveiled and who climbs the mountain passes; when I take off the turban you will know me)
It is said its implied form is: "أنا ابن رجل جلا الأمور" (I am the son of a man who unveiled matters).
There is disagreement about what is implied together with a clause in such as "منّا ظعن ومنا أقام" (among us some departed and some stayed). The Basrans imply a modified noun, i.e. "فريق" (a party). The Kufans imply a relative noun, i.e. "الذي أومن" (the one who...). What the Basrans imply is more in line with analogy, because the connection of the relative noun with its ṣila is stronger than the connection of the modified noun with its adjective, given their mutual inseparability. Similar is "ما منهما مات حتّى لقيته" (none of the two died until I met him): the Basrans imply "أحد" and the Kufans "من". And His saying, Exalted is He, «وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ», i.e. "إلا إنسان" (except a person), or "إلا من". Al-Farrāʾ related from some of their ancients that an oath clause cannot be a ṣila, and he refuted it with His saying, Exalted is He: «وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَ» [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, in the middle of the verse quotation, so the passage ends abruptly in the original.]

safi-cedvel:12-14.t:
* I'rab:
(قبلهم) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to (كذّبت). (كلّ) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: indicated by generality; the tanwīn is a compensation for an omitted element, i.e. "every people of them".], its khabar being the clause كذّب. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (وعيد) is the fāʿil of (حقّ), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on what precedes the omitted yāʾ of the first person, dropped to suit the verse ending (fāṣila), and (الياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كذّبت ... قوم نوح ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كلّ كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كذّب ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ كلّ.
The clause «حقّ وعيد» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كلّ كذّب [Note: or conjoined to the khabar clause, with the linking element implied, i.e. "My threat against him was justified".].

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالخلق) is attached to (عيينا). (بل) is for transitional abandonment. (في لبس) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). (من خلق) is attached to (لبس), as it is made to include the sense of "doubt"..
The clause «عيينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Did We begin the first creation and then become wearied by it?".
The clause «هم في لبس ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(عيينا): it is given in al-Miṣbāḥ: "عيي بالأمر" and "عن حجته" (he was unable regarding the matter, or his argument), يعيا, of the bāb تعب, عيّا: he was incapable of it. The past may be assimilated, so one says عيّ; so the man is عيّ and عييّ, on the patterns فعل (with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn) and فعيل. "عيي بالأمر" means he did not find the way to it. "أعياني" with alif means it wearied me; so "أعييت" is used both intransitively and transitively, and "أعيا في مشيه" (he tired in his walking) gives معيّ, a defective noun.
(لبس) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral لبس of the bāb نصع, i.e. the matter became confused for him. Its pattern is فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
The art of definiteness and indefiniteness: in His saying, Exalted is He, «أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ». He made the first creation definite, and made the confusion (لبس) and the new creation indefinite. Definiteness has no purpose except to magnify and exalt what is meant to be defined; of this is the definiteness of الذكور in His saying «وَيَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الذُّكُورَ». For this purpose the first creation was made definite, because the aim is to make it evidence for the possibility of the second creation a fortiori: if He, Exalted is He, was not wearied by the first creation despite its greatness, then the other creation is the more deserving to be of no concern to Him. This is the secret of the definiteness of the first creation.
As for indefiniteness, it is a divided matter. At times it is meant to magnify the indefinite noun, because of the vagueness in it, as if it were too grand to be addressed as definite; and at times it is meant to belittle and lower the indefinite noun. For the first: (سَلامٌ قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ) and His saying «لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ», which is more than can be counted. The second is the basic rule in indefiniteness, so it needs no illustration. The indefiniteness of اللبس is of magnification and exaltation, as if He had said: "in a confusion, what a confusion"; and the indefiniteness of the new creation is to belittle it and make light of its matter relative to the first creation. It may also be for magnification, as if it were a matter too great for a person to accept being confused about, although the first thing in which its soundness is seen is [Translator's note: the final clause of the source is incomplete or elliptical, "مع أنه أول ما تبصر فيه صحته", and is translated literally as written.].

safi-cedvel:16-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of confirmation. (الواو) is circumstantial. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the direct object [Note: the pronoun in (به) is the returning pronoun ... it is possible that (ما) is a maṣdar particle, with the pronoun in (به) returning to الإنسان, i.e. "the whispering of his soul to him".]. (به) is attached to (توسوس). (الواو) is a conjunction. (إليه) is attached to (أقرب). (من حبل) is attached to (أقرب).
The clause «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.. The implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «نعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "نحن" (we)..
The nominal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl [Note: it is possible that the clause نعلم is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «توسوس» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نحن أقرب ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause (نحن) نعلم.
17- (إذ) is an adverb of past time in the position of accusative attached to (أقرب) [Note: or an adverbial noun in the position of accusative as the direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember).]. (عن اليمين) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (قعيد).. It is singular because it is of the pattern فعيل, in which singular, dual and plural are alike. (عن الشمال) is conjoined to the first prepositional phrase.
The clause «يتلقّى المتلقّيان ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «عن اليمين ... قعيد» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (المتلقّيان).
18- (ما) is negative. (قول) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (إلّا) is for restriction. (لديه) is an indeclinable adverb in the position of accusative attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (رقيب)..
The clause «ما يلفظ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لديه رقيب» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يلفظ.

* Morphology:
(16) الوريد: a name for one of the two veins on the two sides of the neck, the one in which the blood runs to the heart for purification. It is فعيل in the sense of فاعل.
(17) المتلقّيان: the dual of المتلقّي, an active participle from the quinquiliteral form تلقّى. Its pattern is متفعّل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn), with the alif restored to its original yāʾ.
(قعيد) is a resembling adjective from the triliteral قعد, and it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل.
(18) عتيد: a resembling adjective from the triliteral عتد of the bāb كرم in the sense of "was present"; it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl from سكرة, and (الباء) denotes accompaniment [Note: or the bāʾ is for transitivity, so it is attached to (جاءت), i.e. "the stupor of death brought the truth to light".]. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك). (منه) is attached to (تحيد).
The clause «جاءت سكرة الموت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ذلك ما ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of an implied saying, conjoined to the resumption.
The clause «كنت منه تحيد» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تحيد» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنت.

safi-cedvel:20-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (في الصور) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (يوم) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك, nominative.
The clause «نفخ في الصور ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ذلك يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
21- (الواو) is a conjunction. (معها) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (سائق)..
The clause «جاءت كلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نفخ في الصور.
The clause «معها سائق» is in the position of nominative as an adjective (naʿt) of كلّ [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from كلّ نفس ... or in the position of genitive as an adjective of نفس.].
22- (اللام) is the lām of an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of confirmation. (في غفلة) is attached to the khabar of كنت. (من هذا) is attached to (غفلة), as it is made to include the sense of "escape" (najwa) or "deliverance" (najāh). (الفاء) is a conjunction in the two places. (عنك) is attached to (كشفنا). (اليوم) is an adverb of time in the accusative attached to (حديد).
The clause «كنت في غفلة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.. The implied oath clause is in the position of accusative as the content of an implied saying..
The clause «كشفنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
The clause «بصرك اليوم حديد» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كشفنا.
23- (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) from ذا [Note: it may be an indefinite noun that is qualified, a khabar of the mubtadaʾ.. It is also possible that the relative be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is عتيد, and the nominal clause the khabar of the demonstrative.]. (لديّ) is an indeclinable adverb in the position of accusative attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of ما [Note: the adverb may be attached to عتيد if (ما) is an indefinite noun that is qualified and (عتيد) is an adjective of it..
It is also possible that the adverb be an adjective of the qualified indefinite noun and (عتيد) a khabar.]. (عتيد) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هذا [Note: al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal from (ما), or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.].
The clause «قال قرينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied saying clause.
The clause «هذا ... عتيد» is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.

* Morphology:
(21) سائق: an active participle from the triliteral ساق. Its pattern is فاعل, and it involves the substitution of a hamza for its ʿayn; its origin is ساوق.
(22) حديد: a resembling adjective from "حدّت السكين" (the knife was sharp), of the bāb ضرب. Its pattern is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, and it is used in the verse figuratively.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ».
It is a kināya for heedlessness, as if it had covered all of him, or his eyes, so that he sees nothing. When the Day of Resurrection comes he awakens and the heedlessness leaves him, and he sees of the truth what he had not seen.

safi-cedvel:24-26.t:
* I'rab:
(في جهنّم) is attached to (ألقيا). (الخير) is genitive in form by the lām of reinforcement and accusative in position, a direct object of منّاع [Note: it is possible that the preposition is original, attached to منّاع.]. (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ألقياه [Note: it may be a badal from كلّ or a badal from كفّار.]. (مع) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to an omitted second direct object, its governor being جعل. (الفاء) is redundant in the khabar of the relative noun because of its resemblance to a condition. (في العذاب) is attached to (ألقياه)..
The clause «ألقيا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «الذي جعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the content of what precedes.
The clause «جعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «ألقياه ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذي) [Note: it is the apodosis of an implied condition if the relative noun is parsed as a badal.].

* Morphology:
(منّاع) is an intensive form from the triliteral منع. Its pattern is فعّال (with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn).

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) is a vocative muḍāf, accusative. (ما) is negative. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لكن) is for rectification, with no government. (في ضلال) is attached to the khabar of كان.
The clause «قال قرينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said [Note: or parenthetical, with the clause ما أطغيته being the content of what is said.].
The clause «ما أطغيته ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «كان في ضلال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الجنة». It was not made feminine either because it has the sense of «البستان» (the garden), or because the form «فعيل» is not made feminine, since it is of the pattern of verbal nouns; al-Zamakhsharī said this, but the Shaykh did not concede it. What was said earlier on His saying {إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ الله قَرِيبٌ} [الأعراف: 56] spares you this. It is also permissible that it be accusative as an adverbial of place (ẓarf), that is, "a place not far"; and it is permissible that it be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, «إزلافاً غير بعيد» ("a bringing near that is not far"). This is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording, for he said: «or something not far».

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {هذا مَا تُوعَدُونَ}: Two views are permissible for this clause. The first: that it is parenthetical between the badal (substitute) and the one substituted for, because «لكل أَوَّابٍ» is a badal from «للمتقين» with repetition of the governing element. The second: that it is governed by an implied saying, and that saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "it being said to them". It was already mentioned in Sūrat Ṣād that «تُوعَدون» was read with the tāʾ and with the yāʾ. The Shaykh ascribed the reading with the yāʾ (with two dots below) here to Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, but it is in fact from Ibn Kathīr alone.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {مَّنْ خَشِيَ}: It is permissible that it be genitive in position, as a badal (substitute) or a bayān (explicative apposition) of «كل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible that it be a badal after a badal, following «كل»." He means that it is a badal from «كل» after «لكل» was made a badal from «للمتقين»; and he did not make it a further badal of «للمتقين» itself, because the badal is not repeated when the one substituted for is one. It is also permissible that it be a badal for the noun qualified by «أوّاب» and «حفيظ», as al-Zamakhsharī said; he means that the original is «لكل شخصٍ أوّابٍ» ("for every person who is oft-returning"), so «مَنْ خَشِي» would be a badal from the implied «شخص». He said: "It cannot be in the status of «أوّاب» and «حفيظ» (that is, an adjective), because «مَنْ» is not used as an adjective, and among the relative nouns only «الذي» is used as a qualifier." By his saying "in the status of «أوّاب»" he means that «مَنْ» would be made an adjective, and this, as he said, is not permissible. However, the Shaykh took exception to his restriction and said: "Rather, it is qualified by relatives other than «الذي», such as their qualifying with what contains the relative «أل», as in «الضارب» and «المضروب», and such as their qualifying with the two Ṭayyiʾ forms «ذو» and «ذات», as in their saying: «بالفضل ذو فَضَّلكم اللَّهُ به والكرامةِ ذاتُ أكرمكم اللَّهُ بَهْ»."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «مَنْ خَشِي» to be a naʿt (adjective) of what preceded; this is rejected by what has been said. It is also permissible that «مَنْ خَشِي» be nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative by an omitted verb, both by way of qaṭʿ (cutting off), which signals praise; and that it be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is an implied saying that governs His words «ادْخُلوها», that is: "those who feared the Most Merciful, it will be said to them: Enter it." It was first construed according to the wording and in the second place according to the meaning. It was also said that «مَنْ خَشي» is a vocative whose particle of address has been omitted, that is, "O you who feared, enter it," in accordance with the two earlier constructions; and that it be conditional, its apodosis (jawāb) omitted, namely that saying, but with a «فاء» returned with it, that is, «فيقال لهم» ("then it will be said to them"). As for «بالغيب», it is a ḥāl, that is, "unseen by Him"; it may be a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent), from the object, or from both. It was also said that the «باء» is causal, that is, "fear because of the unseen punishment of His with which He threatened"; and it is permissible that it be an adjective of the maṣdar of «خشي», that is, "he feared Him with a fear coupled with the unseen".

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {بِسَلاَمٍ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ادْخلوها», that is, "safe from calamities", in which case it is a concurrent ḥāl; or "greeted with peace upon you", in which case it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), like His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [الزمر: 73]; so it was said. There is room for objection in this, for nothing prevents the angels' greeting of them from coinciding with the time of entering, unlike {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [الزمر: 73], since eternity cannot be conceived except after entering.
His saying: {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخلود}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That is, the time of that is the Day of Eternity," as if he made «ذلك» point to the favour of Allah upon them just mentioned. There is no need for this; rather «ذلك» points to the time that comes after it, as in your saying «هذا زيدٌ» ("this is Zayd").
His saying: {فِيهَا}: It is permissible that it be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَشاؤُون», and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun; the first is preferable.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» is accusative by what follows it. It was put first either because it is interrogative, or because the declarative «كم» is treated like the interrogative in taking the front position. «مِنْ قَرْن» is a tamyīz (specification), and «هم أشدُّ» is an adjective, either of «كم» or of «قرن».
His saying: {فَنَقَّبُواْ}: The «فاء» is a conjunction according to the sense, as if it had been said: "their might was great, so they searched about". The pronoun in «نَقَّبوا» is either for the earlier generations, which is the apparent sense, or for Quraysh. What supports this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Yaʿmar, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Naṣr ibn Sayyār, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Aṣmaʿī on the authority of Abū ʿAmr, «فَنَقِّبوا» with kasra on the «قاف», as a command to them to do so. «التنقيب» is searching and investigating, and its meaning is roaming through the lands. Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza said:
4097 - نَقَّبوا في البلاد مِنْ حَذَرِ الموْ ... تِ وجالُوا في الأرض كلَّ مجَالِ
(They roamed the lands in fear of death, and ranged over the earth in every direction.)
And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4098 - وقد نَقَّبْتُ في الآفاقِ حتى ... رَضِيْتُ مِن الغنيمة بالإِياب
(I have roamed the horizons until I was content, in place of booty, with returning.)
Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAmr also read, in one transmission, «نَقَبوا» with fatḥa on the «قاف», light (without shadda); its meaning is as above. It was also read «نَقِبوا» with kasra, light, that is, their feet and the feet of their camels became weary and bled, the first term of the genitive construct (muḍāf) having been omitted, and that is because of their great roaming.
His saying: {هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is implied, its implied form being: "Is there for whoever follows their path," or "Is there for them any escape?" This clause may or may not be taken as being governed by an implied saying.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {أَوْ أَلْقَى}: The majority read «أَلْقى» in the active voice. Al-Sulamī, Ṭalḥa, al-Suddī and Abū al-Barhasam read «أُلْقِي» in the passive, with «السَّمعُ» made nominative by it. This reading was attributed to ʿĀṣim on the authority of al-Suddī, whom he detested for it and said: "Does He not say «يُلْقُوْن السَّمْعَ»?"

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that it be resumptive. The majority read «اللُّغوب» with ḍamma on the «لام»; ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa, al-Sulamī and Yaʿqūb read it with fatḥa. They are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of the same meaning. This should be added to what Sībawayh reported of the maṣdars that come on this pattern, which are five, and to what al-Kisāʾī added, namely «الوَزُوع», making them seven. I have treated this thoroughly in al-Baqara at His saying {وَقُودُهَا} [الآية: 24].

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {وَأَدْبَارَ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamza read «إِدْبار» with kasra on the hamza, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of an adverbial of time, as in their saying «آتيك خُفوقَ النجمِ وخلافة الحجَّاج» ("I will come to you at the setting of the star and at the caliphate of al-Ḥajjāj"). The meaning is: "at the time of the end of the prayer", that is, its completion and fulfilment. The rest read it with fatḥa, as the plural of «دُبُر», which is the end of the prayer and what follows it; from this is the saying of Aws:
4099 - على دُبُرِ الشهرِ الحَرامِ فأَرْضُنا ... وما حولَها جَدْبٌ سِنونَ تَلْمَعُ
(At the close of the sacred month, our land and what is around it is barren, years of drought glittering.)
They did not differ on {وَإِدْبَارَ النجوم} [الطور: 49].

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {واستمع}: It is listening in its usual sense. It was also said that it means waiting, which is far-fetched. On the first view it is permissible that the object be omitted, that is, "listen for the call of the caller", or "the call of the disbeliever with woe and perdition"; on this «يومَ ينادي» is an adverbial of time for «استمع», that is, "listen for that on a day...".
It was also said: "listen to what I say to you." On this «يومَ يُنادي» is accusative by an implied «يَخْرجون» ("they will come out"), indicated by His saying {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخروج} [ق: 42]; and on the second view (waiting) «يومَ ينادي» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is, "await that day".
Ibn Kathīr paused on «يُنادي» with the yāʾ, while the others paused without it. The reason for retaining it is that nothing requires its omission; the reason for omitting it in pausing is to follow the written form, and pausing is a place for lightening. As for «المنادي», Ibn Kathīr also retained its yāʾ both in continuous reading and in pausing; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retained it in continuous reading and omitted it in pausing; and the rest of the Seven omitted it in both. Whoever retained it did so because it is the original form; whoever omitted it did so to follow the written form; and whoever restricted the omission to pausing did so because pausing is a place of rest and a place of change.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ}: a badal (substitute) from «يومَ ينادي». «بالحق» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصيحة», that is, "coupled with the truth", or from the fāʿil (agent), that is, "they hear, coupled with a true hearing".
His saying: {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخروج}: It is permissible that the implied sense be "that time", that is, the time of the call and the hearing is the Day of Coming Out. It is also permissible that «ذلك» point to the call, in which case latitude has been taken with the adverbial so that it is predicated of the maṣdar (verbal noun); or a muḍāf (annexed noun) is implied before that call and hearing: "the call of the Day of Coming Out and its hearing".

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ}: «يوم» may be a badal (substitute) from the «يوم» before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a badal from the first «يوم»." There is room for objection in this, because the badal would be repeated while the one substituted for is one; and it has already been mentioned that al-Zamakhsharī forbade it. It is also permissible that the day be an adverbial for «المصير» (the return). It was also said: an adverbial for the coming out. It was also said: accusative by an implied «يَخْرُجون». The disagreement about «يَشَّقَّقُ» was mentioned in al-Furqān. Zayd read «تَتَشَقَّق» with the doubling undone.
His saying: {سِرَاعاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عنهم», and the operator on it is «تَشَقَّقُ». It was also said that its operator is the one operating on the implied «يوم تَشَقَّقُ», that is, «يَخْرُجون سِراعاً يوم تَشَقَّقُ» ("they will come out hastening on the day it splits open").
His saying: {عَلَيْنَا}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسير», so the object of the adjective separates between it and what it qualifies, and this does no harm. It is also permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from it, because originally it may be an adjective. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fronting is for restriction, that is, that is not easy except for Allah alone." The disagreement about the yāʾ of «وعيد», retained or omitted, was mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {والقرآن}: an oath. There are several views about its answer. The first: that it is His saying {قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ الأرض}. The second: {مَا يُبَدَّلُ القول}. The third: {مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ}. The fourth: {إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لذكرى}. The fifth: {بَلْ عجبوا}, which is a Kufan view; they said: because it is equivalent to «قد عَجِبوا». The sixth: that it is omitted; al-Zajjāj, al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad supplied «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» ("you will surely be resurrected"). ʿĪsā read «ق» with fatḥa, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq with kasra, and Hārūn and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ with ḍamma. The justification of all that has already passed: the fatḥa allows that it is indeclinable on fatḥa for lightness, or accusative by an implied verb and a diptote, or genitive by an implied oath particle, also a diptote. The ḍamma is on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ or a khabar, also a diptote.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أَإِذَا مِتْنَا}: the majority read it with the interrogative; Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash and al-Aʿraj read it with one hamza, which allows the interrogative, as with the majority, the particle being omitted because it is indicated, and also allows a statement of fact. The operator of the adverbial in the majority reading is implied, that is: "Shall we be resurrected, or shall we return, when we have died?" The apodosis of «إذا» in the reading as a statement is omitted, that is: "we shall return." It is also said that it is His saying «ذلك رَجْعٌ» with the fāʾ omitted, which is the view of some; the majority permit this only in poetry. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that «الرَّجْعُ», meaning «المَرْجوع», is the answer, and is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, expressing the improbability of their denial of what they were warned of regarding the resurrection. Pausing at what precedes it is good on this interpretation." If you ask: what then governs the adverbial if «الرَّجْعُ» means «المَرْجوع»? I say: what is indicated by the warner of the thing warned of, namely the resurrection." The Shaykh attacked him for understanding it so.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {بَلْ كَذَّبُواْ}: this is a second iḍrāb (turning from one statement to another). al-Zamakhsharī said: "An iḍrāb that follows the previous iḍrāb, to indicate that they came with something more shocking than their wonder, namely denying the truth." The Shaykh said: "It is as if this second iḍrāb were a substitute of retraction (badal badāʾ) for the first." I say: to apply such a term in the Book of Allah is not permissible at all. It is also said: before this verse there is a sentence turned away from, its implied form being: "They did not look well; rather they denied." What al-Zamakhsharī said is better.
The majority read «لَمَّا» with doubling, and it is either a particle of necessity for necessity, or an adverbial meaning "when", as you know. al-Jaḥdarī read it with kasra on the lām and the mīm light, on the basis that it is the lām of the genitive entering the maṣdar «ما», parallel to their saying «كتبْتُه لخمسٍ خَلَوْن» ("I wrote it on the fifth, the days having passed"), that is, at it.
His saying: {مَّرِيجٍ}: that is, confused. Abū Wāqid said:
4089 - مَرِجَ الدِّيْنُ فأَعْدَدْتُ له ... مُشْرِفَ الأَقْطارِ مَحْبوكَ الكَتَدْ
(Religion fell into disorder, so I prepared for it a tall-framed horse, with a well-knit withers.)
Another said:
4090 - فجالَتْ والتمسْتُ به حَشاها ... فَخَرَّ كأنَّه خُوْطٌ مَرِيْجُ
(She wheeled, and I sought her flank with it; he fell like a restless shoot.)
Its origin is from movement and agitation / and from it: «مَرَجَ الخاتمُ في إصبعِه» ("the ring was loose on his finger").

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {فَوْقَهُمْ}: a ḥāl from «السماء», and it is an emphatic one. And «كيف» is accusative by what follows it [source: «بعجها»] and it suspends the "looking" before it. [Translator's note: the source reads «بعجها»; this appears to be a misprint for «بعدها» ("after it"), and the translation follows that sense.]

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {تَبْصِرَةً}: the majority put it in the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is: "to give insight to people like them and as a reminder from Us to them." It is also said: both are accusative by a verb of their own wording, implied, that is: "Give them insight, an insight, and remind them, a reminder." It is also said: two ḥāls, that is: "given insight, reminded". It is also said: a ḥāl from the object, that is: "possessing insight and reminder for whoever sees it." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the nominative. He read «وذِكْرٌ», that is: "it is an insight and a reminder." And «لكلِّ» is either an adjective or attached to the maṣdar itself.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَحَبَّ الحصيد}: it may be a case of omitting the described noun because it is known, the implied form being: «وحَبَّ الزَرْعِ الحصيدِ» ("the grain of the harvested crop"), like «مسجد الجامع» and similar. This is the school of the Basrans, so that the annexation of a thing to itself is not necessary. It may also be a case of annexing the described noun to its adjective, because the original is «والحَبَّ الحصيدَ», that is, the harvested.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {والنخل}: accusative, conjoined to the object of «أَنْبَتْنا», that is: "and We caused the palm trees to grow." And «باسِقاتٍ» is a ḥāl, an anticipated one (muqaddara), since at the time of their growth they were not tall. «البُسُوْقُ» is height. One says «بَسَقَ فلانٌ على أصحابِه», that is, he towered over his companions in excellence. From it is the saying of Ibn Nawfal about Ibn Hubayra: 4091 - يا بنَ الذين بمَجْدِهمْ ... بَسَقَتْ على قَيْسٍ فَزارَهْ
(O son of those by whose glory Fazāra towered over Qays.)
It is a metaphor; the original usage is in «بَسَقَتِ النخلةُ تَبْسُق بُسُوْقاً», that is, it grew tall. The poet said:
4092 - لنا خَمْرٌ وليسَتْ خمرَ كَرْمٍ ... ولكنْ مِنْ نِتاجِ الباسِقاتِ
كِرامٌ في السماءِ ذَهَبْنَ طُوْلاً ... وفاتَ ثمارَها أيدي الجُناةِ
(We have wine, though not the wine of vines, but from the produce of the tall palms: noble ones that went up high in the sky, their fruit beyond the hands of the pickers.)
«بَسَقَتِ الشاةُ» means the ewe gave birth; «أَبْسَقَت الناقةُ» means the colostrum came into her udder before delivery, and from that «نوقٌ مَباسِيْقُ». The majority read it with sīn. Qutba ibn Mālik, who reports it from the Prophet ﷺ, read «باصِقاتٍ» with ṣād, which is a dialect of Banū l-ʿAnbar, who replace sīn with ṣād before qāf, ghayn, khāʾ and ṭāʾ when these follow it, or are separated from it by one or two letters.
His saying: {لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ}: the sentence may be a ḥāl from «النخل» or from the pronoun in «باسِقاتٍ»; it may also be that the ḥāl is «لها» alone, with «طَلْعٌ» its agent, and «نَضِيْدٌ» in the sense of «مَنْضود» (stacked).

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {رِّزْقاً}: it may be a ḥāl, that is, "provision for the servants", i.e. possessing provision; it may be a maṣdar from the meaning of «أَنْبَتْنا», because the growing of this is provision; and it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. And «للعباد» is either an adjective, or attached to the maṣdar, or an object of the maṣdar with a redundant lām, that is: "provision for the servants."
His saying: {بِهِ}: that is, with the water. And «مَيْتاً» is an adjective of «بَلْدة». It was not made feminine, considering the meaning of place. The majority read it light. Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid read it heavy.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {الأيكة}: it has been discussed in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it here as «لَيْكَة» on the pattern of «لَيْلَة». The Shaykh said: "Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ṭalḥa and Nāfiʿ read «الأَيْكةِ» with the definite lām, and the majority «لَيْكَة»." What he reported is a lapse of his; rather the well-known disagreement is only in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ and Ṣād, as I verified there; but here the majority read it with the definite lām.
His saying: {كُلٌّ}: the tanwīn is a replacement for the omitted muḍāf ilayhi. Some grammarians allowed dropping its tanwīn and making it indeclinable on ḍamma, as the majority do with «قبل» and «بعد».

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {أَفَعَيِينَا}: the majority read it with a yāʾ with kasra followed by a quiescent yāʾ. Its meaning has already passed in al-Aḥqāf. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أفَعَيِّنا» with the yāʾ doubled without lengthening. This reading, for all its difficulty, was read by al-Walīd ibn Muslim, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ in one transmission, and Ibn Khālawayh reported from Ibn Abī ʿAbla «أفَعَيِّينا» likewise, but he brought a further quiescent yāʾ after the doubled yāʾ. The Shaykh explained it on the dialect of those who say «عَيِيَ» → «عَيَّ», and «حَيِيَ» → «حَيَّ», with assimilation. Then, when this verb is predicated while assimilated, and the dialect of Bakr ibn Wāʾil is taken into account, namely that they do not undo the assimilation in such a case when they predicate the assimilated verb to the speaker's tāʾ, or any of its sisters for which the lām of the verb becomes quiescent, so they say of «رَدَّ»: «رَدْتُ» and «رَدْنا», he said: "on this dialect / the yāʾ is with fatḥa." I say: he did not mention the justification of the other reading. Its justification is that it is from «عَيَّا يُعَيِّي» like «حَلَّى يُحَلِّي».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وَنَعْلَمُ}: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "and We know"; the nominal sentence is then a ḥāl. It cannot be a ḥāl by itself, because it is an affirmative imperfect directly preceded by the wāw. Likewise His saying «ونحن أقربُ».
His saying: {مِنْ حَبْلِ الوريد}: this is like their saying «مسجد الجامع», that is, the cord of the jugular vein; or because «الحبل» is more general, to clarify, as in «بعير سانية»; or the cord of the shoulder (ʿātiq) is intended, and so it is annexed to the vein as it is annexed to the shoulder, because both are in one limb. «الوريد» is either in the sense of «الوارد» or in the sense of «المورود». «الوريد» is a large vein in the neck; it is said that there are two jugular veins. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Two veins enclosing the two sides of the neck at the front, joined to the aorta (watīn); they come down from the head to it. It is called warīd because the spirit comes (tarid) to it." And he recited:
4093 - كأنْ وَرِيْدَيْهِ رِشاءُ خُلْبِ
(As if his two jugular veins were a rope of palm fibre.)
al-Athram said: "It is the river of the body: in the heart it is the watīn, in the back the abhar, in the arm and thigh the akḥal and the nasā, and in the little finger the aslam."

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى}: an adverbial of «أَقْرَبُ». It may also be accusative by "remember".
His saying: {عَنِ اليمين وَعَنِ الشمال قَعِيدٌ}: it may be singular on its usual sense, so it means «مُفاعِل» like «خليط» in the sense of «مُخالِط»; or it may be shifted from «فاعِل» to «فعيل» for intensity, like «عليم». The Kufans allowed «فعيل» to stand in the place of two. al-Mubarrad said: "The original is: 'on the right a sitter and on the left'; so it was postponed from its place." This does not escape the singular standing in the place of the dual. The better course is to claim an omission, either from the first, that is: "on the right a sitter and on the left a sitter", or from the second, so that the pronounced «قعيدٌ» belongs to the first. Similar is the saying of another:
4094 - رَماني بأَمْرٍ كنتُ منه ووالدي ... بَريئاً ومِنْ أجل الطَّوِيِّ رَماني
(He accused me of a matter of which I and my father were innocent, and on account of the well he accused me.)

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {مَّا يَلْفِظُ}: the majority read it with kasra on the fāʾ, and Muḥammad ibn Abī Maʿdān with fatḥa. «رقيبٌ عتيدٌ» is said to mean «رقيبان عتيدان» (two watchers, ready).

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {بالحق}: the bāʾ may be of ḥāl, that is, "joined with the truth", and it may be of transitivity. ʿAbd Allāh read «سَكَراتُ». «تَحيد» means "you incline", from «حادَ عن الشيء يَحيد حُيُوداً وحُيُوْدَة وحَيْداً».

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌ}: a sentence in the genitive position as an adjective of «نَفْسٍ», or in the nominative as an adjective of «كل», or in the accusative as a ḥāl from «كلُّ». The majority read «معها» without assimilation; Ṭalḥa read it with assimilation, «مَحَّا» with a doubled ḥāʾ; that is, he assimilated the ʿayn into the hāʾ, which is not possible, so he turned the hāʾ into ḥāʾ, then assimilated the ʿayn into it, turning it into ḥāʾ. «ذَهَبَ مَحُّمْ», that is, «معهم», was heard. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The position of «معها سائقٌ» is accusative as ḥāl from «كلُّ», because it is made definite by annexation to what is in the status of a definite." The Shaykh attacked him, as is his habit, saying: "A beginner in grammar would not say this, because if «كلُّ نفس» were qualified, it would be qualified only by an indefinite." This is unbecoming of him, since he knows that he did not mean literally what he said.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {لَّقَدْ كُنتَ}: that is, it is said to him: "You were indeed...", and the saying is either an adjective or a ḥāl. The majority read fatḥa on the tāʾ and the kāf in «كنتَ», «غِطاءَكَ» and «فبصَرُك», following the masculine wording of «كلُّ». al-Jaḥdarī read «كنتِ» with kasra, addressing the soul; he and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «عنكِ», «غطاءَكِ», «فبصَرُكِ» with kasra, also taking the soul into account. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» did not report the kasra of the kāf from al-Jaḥdarī; in sum, he took the wording into account in one place and the meaning in another.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {هذا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ}: «ما» may be an indefinite described noun, «عتيدٌ» its adjective, and «لَدَيَّ» attached to «عتيدٌ», that is: "this is a thing ready with me", i.e. present with me. On this «لديَّ» may be a description of «ما», with «عتيدٌ» a second adjective, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "it is ready." It may also be a relative noun meaning "that which"; «لَدَيَّ» is its ṣila and «عتيدٌ» the khabar of the relative, and the relative with its ṣila is the khabar of the demonstrative. It may also be that «ما» is a badal from «هذا», whether relative or described by «لَدَيَّ», with «عتيدٌ» the khabar of «هذا». al-Zamakhsharī allowed «عَتيدٌ» to be a badal, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. / The majority read it in the nominative; ʿAbd Allāh put it in the accusative as a ḥāl. The better course then is that «ما» be relative, because it is definite, and ḥāl often comes from a definite. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had this occurred outside the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to put it in the accusative as a ḥāl." I say: what he wished has come, thanks be to Allah; it seems he did not come across it as a reading.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {أَلْقِيَا}: they differed: is the one commanded one or two? Some said: one, and the dual pronoun was used to indicate repetition of the act, as if it were said: "Cast, cast." It is also said: he meant «أَلْقِيَنْ» with the light nūn, and replaced it with an alif, treating continuation like pause; this is supported by al-Ḥasan's reading «أَلْقِيَنْ» with the nūn.
It is also said: the Arabs address one person as they address two, for emphasis, as in:
4095 - فإن تَزْجُراني يا بنَ عَفَّانَ أَزْدَجِرْ ... وإنْ تَدَعاني أَحْمِ عِرْضاً مُمَنَّعا
(If you two rebuke me, O Ibn ʿAffān, I will desist; and if you two leave me alone, I will protect a well-guarded honour.)
And another said:
4096 - فقُلْتُ لصاحبي لا تَحْبِسانا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I said to my companion: "Do not you two hold us back...")
the verse. Some said: the one commanded is a dual. This is the truth, because what is meant is two angels who do that.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {الذي جَعَلَ}: it may be accusative for censure, or as a badal from «كل»; or genitive as a badal from «كَفَّار»; or nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «فَأَلْقياه» as the khabar. It is said that the fāʾ entered because of its likeness to a condition. It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "he is the one who made", and «فَأَلْقِياه» would then be an emphasis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to be an adjective of «الكَفَّار», saying: "inasmuch as «كَفَّار» is specific to the mentioned attributes, it is permissible to qualify it with this definite." This is rejected. It was also read with fatḥa on the tanwīn, to avoid the succession of four similar letters.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {قَالَ قَرِينُهُ}: this came without a wāw because resumption is intended by it, as if the disbeliever had said: "My Lord, he made me transgress", and his companion said: "I did not make him transgress"; unlike the one before it, which is conjoined to what precedes it to indicate the combination of its meaning and the meaning of what precedes in occurrence, I mean the coming of «كلُّ نفس» with the two angels and the saying of his companion what he said to him.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {قَالَ لاَ تَخْتَصِمُواْ}: also resumptive, as if someone asked: "What did Allah say to him?" and it was answered: «قال: لا تَخْتصموا».
His saying: {وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ}: a ḥāl clause. It requires interpretation, for the prohibition is in the Hereafter and the advance warning was in the world, so the two times differ; how then can it be made a ḥāl? Its interpretation is that the meaning is "and it has been established that I gave advance warning", and the time of establishment and the time of the prohibition are the same. «قَدَّمْتُ» may be in the sense of «تَقَدَّمْتُ», so the tāʾ is of ḥāl, and a muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "and My word to you has preceded, joined with the warning." It may also be that «قَدَّمْتُ» is transitive as it is, with the bāʾ redundant in the object, that is: "I gave you advance warning of the threat."

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ نَقُولُ}: «يوم» is accusative, either by «ظَلاَّم», but this has no implication, because if He does not wrong on this day, the negation of wrong on other days is all the more so; or by His saying {وَنُفِخَ فِي الصور} [Qāf: 20], the pointing "that" referring to «يومَ نقول»; said by al-Zamakhsharī, and the Shaykh found it remote because of the many intervening elements; or by an implied "remember", or by "warn", and on these last two it is a direct object, not an adverbial.
His saying: {هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ}: a question of affirmation and making them stand to account. It is also said: its meaning is negation. It is also said: the question is put to its keepers, and the answer is from them, so a muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "We say to the keepers of Hell, and they say", then he omitted it. Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read «يقول لجهنمَ» with the third-person yāʾ, the agent being Allah the Exalted, since He was mentioned earlier in His saying «مع الله»; the others read with the nūn of the speaker glorifying himself, since He was mentioned earlier in «لديَّ» and «وقد قَدَّمْتُ». al-Aʿmash read «يُقال» as a passive. «المزيد» may be a maṣdar, and may be a passive participle, that is: "Is there anything you add for Me that I might burn?"

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ (١) بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جَاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَقَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ هَذَا شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ (٢) أَئِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ (٣)).
Whoever says that (ق) is an oath makes the wāw in (وَالْقُرْآنِ) a conjunction; for whoever says otherwise, it is the wāw of the oath. The apodosis of the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted. It is said that it is His saying: (قَدْ عَلِمْنَا . . . (٤)), i.e. لَقَدْ, the lām having been dropped because of the length of the speech.
It is also said that it is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected" (لَتُبْعَثُنَّ) or "you will surely be returned" (لَتُرْجَعُنَّ), according to what the context of the verses indicates.
And (بَلْ) is for moving from one story to another. And (إِذَا) is accusative by what the answer indicates, i.e. "shall we return?"

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَعْلَمُ), i.e. "while We know", so the clause is a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated circumstantial). It may also be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى الْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ (١٧) مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى) may be an adverb (ẓarf) for أَقْرَبُ, or the implied wording may be "remember".
And (قَعِيدٌ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عَنِ الشِّمَالِ» is its khabar (predicate); this «قَعِيدٌ» indicates the first «قَعِيدٌ», i.e. "on the right is one seated".
It is also said that the «قَعِيدٌ» mentioned is the first, and the second is omitted.
It is also said that there is no omission: قَعِيدٌ means "two seated ones", the singular sufficing for the dual; parallels to this have passed before. And (رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ) is singular in wording, while the meaning is "two watchers, ready".

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْحَقِّ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ (٢١) لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنْكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ): the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of نَفْس, or of كُلّ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كُلّ; this is permissible because of the generality in it. And the implied wording is: "it will be said to him: لَقَدْ كُنْتَ …", the masculine being used according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُ هَذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Regarding «مَا» there are two views. First: it is indefinite, and «عَتِيدٌ» is its adjective (ṣifa), and «لَدَيَّ» is governed by عَتِيد.
«لَدَيَّ» may also be an adjective too, so it is attached to something omitted; and «مَا» with its adjective is the khabar (predicate) of هَذَا.
The second view: «مَا» means "that which" (al-ladhī); on this view «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ, «لَدَيَّ» is the ṣila (relative clause), «عَتِيدٌ» is the khabar of «مَا», and the clause is the khabar of «هَذَا». «مَا» may also be a badal (substitute) for هَذَا.
«عَتِيدٌ» may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, with «مَا لَدَيَّ» being the khabar of «هَذَا», i.e. "it is ready". Had that occurred outside the Quran, its accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلْقِيَا), i.e. that will be said. Regarding the dual form here there are several views. First: it is an address to the two angels. Second: it is to one, and the alif is a substitute for repeating the verb, i.e. "throw, throw" (أَلْقِ أَلْقِ).
Third: it is to one, but it came out in the dual form according to their custom, as in their sayings خَلِيلِيَّ عُوجَا ("my two friends, turn aside") and خَلِيلِيَّ مُرَّا بِي ("my two friends, pass by me with me"); that is because the usual state of one of them is that two companions accompany him on a journey. Fourth: some of the Arabs address one person with the address of two, as in the poet's saying:
فَإِنْ تَزْجُرَانِي يَا بْنَ عَفَّانَ أَنْزَجِرْ ... وَإِنْ تَدَعَانِي أَحْمِ عِرْضًا مُمَنَّعًا
(If you [two] restrain me, O son of ʿAffān, I will be restrained; and if you [two] leave me, I will defend an honour well protected.)
